title: Future Trends of the Distribution System in the Cinema Entertainment Industry: Application of Cognitive Mapping Approach

detail.title: Future Trends of the Distribution System in the Cinema Entertainment Industry: Application of Cognitive Mapping Approach

detail.abstract: Introduction: The entertainment industry has emerged as a pivotal sector in the global economy, with its distribution systems playing a crucial role in shaping both its operations and evolution. Cinema, as a central component of this industry, possesses a distinctive distribution system that has historically experienced substantial transformations due to technological advancements and global dynamics. This research seeks to examine future trends and scenarios related to cinema distribution, with a particular focus on the Iranian context and its unique challenges and opportunities. Method: This study employs a qualitative methodology, utilizing Cognitive Mapping (CM) as a problem-structuring tool. Through focused group discussions with ten industry experts, the research identifies and conceptualizes future trends within Iran's cinema distribution system. The cognitive mapping technique facilitates the development of a visual conceptual model illustrating the relationships among trends, scenarios, and their interdependencies. Results: The findings reveal five major predictable trends: (1) changes in service delivery modalities, (2) enhanced strategies for audience engagement and retention, (3) infrastructural transformations, (4) evolution in content types, and (5) shifts in distribution channels. These trends are anticipated to significantly influence the future of cinema distribution in Iran, offering valuable insights into emerging scenarios and potential challenges. Moreover, the study underscores how these trends interact and overlap, forming a complex network of opportunities and constraints for stakeholders. Conclusion: The results highlight the necessity of strategic foresight and proactive planning for cinema policymakers and industry managers. By comprehending these trends and their interrelations, stakeholders can better navigate future developments and design adaptive strategies to sustain competitiveness in the rapidly evolving entertainment landscape. The concluding sections of the research elaborate on the detailed relationships among the five identified trends, providing actionable insights for practical implementation in Iran's cinema distribution ecosystem.

detail.abstract: We study labour-market entry and career progression among 424 alumni of Quantitative Finance and Insurance and its predecessors at the University of Turin, using monthly career histories reconstructed from public LinkedIn profiles. Ninety-three hold a qualifying job at graduation. Among 331 others, median time to the first observed qualifying job is five months, and 73.1% enter by month 12. Most observed first jobs involve actuarial science, insurance, risk, finance, investment, or banking. Alumni with relevant pre-graduation experience tend to enter these occupations more quickly. In a small, non-random recent-cohort comparison, the 12-month employment share is 31% higher among alumni with a recorded during-degree internship. A full-horizon analysis of 371 careers identifies broad technical, managerial, and director-oriented patterns. These recur over a shared five-year window, while individual assignments and finer distinctions remain sensitive to model choices. Self-reported histories and unequal follow-up limit causal and person-level interpretations.

detail.abstract: The US tariffs imposed on Chinese goods under Section 301 in 2018-2019 triggered a large reallocation of US imports away from China, and nearshoring narratives predicted that Latin America, closer to the US market, would be a principal beneficiary. This article tests that prediction with product-level US import data for 74 major suppliers, 4,772 HS6 products and the years 2015-2025, combined with the original tariff lists published in the Federal Register and the World Bank Logistics Performance Index. Using Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood with exporter-product, product-year and exporter-year fixed effects, the estimates show that a full 25-point tariff increase reduced China's imports by about half relative to other suppliers, with flat pre-trends. Latin American exporters did not capture a disproportionate share of this diversion: in tariffed products their imports fell by about 27% relative to other non-Chinese suppliers, a result that holds for Mexico, Central America and South America separately and survives alternative windows, samples and treatment definitions. Pre-shock logistics performance does not explain which Latin American countries fared better; the moderation estimate is fragile and its randomization-inference p-value is 0.44. Proximity and logistics capacity were not sufficient conditions for capturing tariff-driven reallocation.

title: Designed for the User, Sold to the Buyer: How Far Does User-centred Design Affect Marketing Effectiveness and Consumer Purchase Intention in Contemporary Product Design?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Designed for the User, Sold to the Buyer: How Far Does User-centred Design Affect Marketing Effectiveness and Consumer Purchase Intention in Contemporary Product Design?

detail.abstract:
User-centred design (UCD) is regularly claimed to boost marketing performance and large numbers of headline
figures are referenced to support this. The facts of academia tell a more qualified story. This paper therefore
questions the degree of impact UCD has on marketing effectiveness and the consumers' purchase intention,
and identifies the conditions in which the impact is robust, weak or null.
A structured review brings together three layers of evidence that are typically not read together: firm level
design-performance indices, consumer level psychometric studies of design perception and intention and large-
scale behavioural data at the point of purchase. Extraction, comparison and evaluation of reported effect sizes
with the range of effect sizes that are allowed by each research design.
There are three noteworthy results. Firstly, there is a strong indirect pathway, the indirect pathway being the
effect of design on perceived value, perceived usefulness and affective response, and the direct pathway weak
or insignificant when mediators are modelled. Secondly the relative importance of the mediators is context
sensitive (commercially). A meta-analysis of 88 studies found that the direct effect of perceived ease of use on
intention is approximately 2½ times greater in the internet and e-commerce environment (beta = 0.258) than
in the job environment (beta = 0.098); the perceived usefulness direct effect is the converse of this. The
experiential ease is most important in the consumer-facing markets. Third, the financial evidence for design
investment, which is typically cited in support of design investment, is generally correlational, collected from
a selected group of companies or from self-reported surveys, and is inconsistently reported from the original,
for example, two widely cited figures are traced back to their originals and it is shown that they have drifted
in transmission.
The paper provides an integrated mediation model, nine propositions for testing, a moderator model that
differentiates search goods, experience goods and credence goods, and a citation-integrity audit of the design-
value evidence base. Its key message is that UCD has a significant, but limited, indirect and qualitative impact
on marketing outcomes and that hyperbole can be counterproductive to the UCD argument, while understating
it can be damaging.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes the Keel-and-Compass Model, a management framework that treats ethics as a preservation discipline rather than a compliance task. Every significant decision passes two tests in fixed order: the Keel, a Kantian floor of universalizability, dignity and publicity, and the Compass, a utilitarian ranking of the remaining options by reach, harm and unrepresented stakeholders. When the tests cannot be reconciled, a leader chosen for fitness rather than seniority makes a signed, logged call that a council with bounded power can review. Building on the author's earlier work on family preservation structures, economic resilience and competition policy, the model treats trust, relationships and knowledge as capital that decays without maintenance. It is specified for marketing and human resources teams in physical, digital and hybrid settings, with a nonprofit track that uses published decision logs and multi-capital reporting as trust signals for donors. The paper presents the model, its philosophical grounding, worked examples, a practice case, further thoughts on management, a fair definition of merit, guidance, formulas and positive examples for applying the model in any business, a general guide to applying it across every area of management, practical structures for turning principles into action, a management competency model, measures, a rollout and pilot design, and testable propositions.

detail.abstract: Nowadays, advertising has become an inseparable part of human social life. Because in order to sell products, ideas, and also to spread a thought or innovation, we need people's support and persuasion, and accordingly we need to advertise about the desired products or ideas and thoughts. But one of the shortcomings of Islamic societies in the contemporary era is the methods of advertising based on religious values and teachings. In the field of advertising from the point of view of Islam, there have been works and researches, although negative, but there is no written and comprehensive research or work that summarizes the opinions raised in the field of advertising based on Islam; Therefore, the current research is looking for the comprehensive methods and strategies of Islamic promotion as well as the limitations of religion from the perspective of the Quran and hadiths. In this research, the researchers referred to the authentic Islamic sources using the meta synthesis method and finally, among the 430 initial articles obtained, 19 suitable articles for this topic were discovered and used, which were further analyzed to code and identify the basic, organizing themes. And it was comprehensive. Also, using the literature of communication science, the message transmission process was divided into three parts: the sender, the message content, and the message receiver. In this research, it has been tried to categorize and present the instructions and methods of promotion approved by Islam in the verses and traditions according to these three parts.

detail.abstract: Industrial agriculture is the modernized, large-scale form of growing crops with intensive means to maximize yield for profit, but it is often associated with costly economic and environmental consequences. Sustainable alternatives to intensification include using multiple cropping systems and technological innovation to increase crop yield while minimizing cost to farmers and ecological damage. Although industrial agriculture is designed to provide short-term yields, its long-term environmental and economic consequences outweigh these benefits, and transitioning away from current methods is necessary and feasible if farmers receive the support needed to implement these changes. The land use practices utilized by industrial agriculture in the form of monocropping cause widespread ecological damage, whereas more sustainable systems could be implemented to help mitigate these consequences and reduce costs to farmers. Similarly, pesticide use helps prevent loss of crop yields, but because of the extent of its harm to the environment and human health, industrial agriculture would benefit from more sustainable pest control practices. Though there is scientific evidence behind many more sustainable practices, there are many political and cultural practices that currently stand in the way of their implementation. One of the most prominent of these challenges is a belief that sustainable practices could threaten higher crop yields, but technological innovations may instead improve the efficiency of industrial agriculture in the face of climate change. While sustainable practices have the potential to solve the issues that have been presented, there are trade-offs for any agricultural practice that must be analyzed in order to find reasonable compromises that benefit both farmers and consumers. Our main finding is that the benefits of industrial farming, such as short-term efficiency and higher seasonal yields, are outweighed by the economic, financial, and nutritional downsides that arise as negative externalities. There is a lack of adaptation to multiple cropping systems and alternative technologies due to insufficient financial support, and farmers are unlikely to act for the good of humanity when they are expected to bear the risk of technological failure amid increasing pressure from population growth. Farmers are hesitant to stray from tradition due to a lack of economic and social support from politicians, corporations, and consumers, but this assistance could provide a buffer for adaptation to adjust to more sustainable alternative practices.

detail.abstract:
Selection decisions — who to field as a political candidate, which founder to back, which brand name will resonate, which executive will carry an organisation through disruption, which public policy will achieve popular acceptance — are among the most consequential and least scientifically grounded judgements that individuals and institutions make. They are currently dominated by intuition, ideology, tribal loyalty, and narrative momentum, with limited systematic recourse to the psychosocial science of why certain people, ideas, and identities achieve winning resonance with specific populations at specific moments.

This paper introduces the Winnability Quotient (WQ) as a psychosocial base model for evaluating winning potential across selection contexts. WQ is defined as the population's composite psychosocial readiness to confer recognition, preference, and ultimately selection on a candidate entity — whether a person, a brand, a policy, or an idea — in a specific competitive context. It is explicitly positioned as a foundational model: a theoretically grounded, empirically referable, and practically orienting framework intended to invite systematic extension, empirical testing, and domain-specific refinement by researchers, practitioners, and tool developers. It is a nudge, not a verdict; a base for further inquiry, not a terminal algorithm.

The WQ framework rests on five psychosocial pillars derived from convergent bodies of social psychology, cognitive science, embodied cognition, cultural psychology, and — uniquely — Indic epistemological theory: Perceived Competence Signal (P₁), Identity Resonance Score (P₂), Narrative Congruence Index (P₃), Somatic Trust Signal (P₄), and Contextual Adversity Quotient (P₅). These five pillar scores interact with a Cultural Calibration Coefficient (C) and a Temporal Alignment Factor (T) to produce the composite WQ. The model is operationalised across five domain-specific application scenarios: political candidate selection, startup founder investment, brand-to-market acceptability, executive leadership appointment, and public policy acceptance. Each scenario specifies the pillar weightings, measurement approaches, and interpretive constraints appropriate to its context.

The paper draws explicitly on the Indic Futures Paper Series (Bandvi, 2026a–2026g) — particularly the Indic Cognitive Resilience Model's account of how populations evaluate identity resonance, the Want Architecture's account of how resonance is engineered versus genuine, and the Dharmic Algorithm Protocol's epistemological standard for reliable assessment. It positions WQ as a complement to, not a replacement for, human judgment: a structured framework for making the relevant psychosocial variables visible and systematic so that selection decisions can be made with greater awareness of what they are actually responding to.

Not peer-reviewed. Circulated for scholarly discussion and further development. APA 7. AI Disclosure: AI-based tools assisted with literature organisation and language editing. All framework design, constructs, and conclusions are the author's own.

title: Retirement Decumulation as a Coordination Problem: Consumer Preferences, Market Trade-Offs, and Policy Implications
affiliations: KU Leuven, University of Esslingen and University of Mannheim - Department of Banking and Finance

detail.title: Retirement Decumulation as a Coordination Problem: Consumer Preferences, Market Trade-Offs, and Policy Implications

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

affiliations.org_name: University of Mannheim - Department of Business Administration and Finance

detail.abstract: Population aging increases pressure on pay-as-you-go pension systems and shifts responsibility for retirement income toward individuals. Yet little is known about how consumers value key attributes of decumulation products and whether these preferences align with financial trade-offs and policy objectives. We study decumulation as a multistakeholder coordination problem involving consumers, financial service providers, and policy makers. Using a choice-based conjoint experiment calibrated with Monte Carlo simulations of realistic drawdown strategies, we quantify how individuals trade off monthly consumption, risk of running out of wealth, consumption volatility, and endof-horizon wealth. We document three main findings. First, end-of-horizon wealth is the dominant attribute, while the risk of running out and consumption volatility receive lower importance weights. Second, consumers' willingness-to-pay for end-ofhorizon wealth exceeds market-consistent trade-offs, indicating positive surplus potential that providers can exploit through capital-market-based products. A latent segmentation reveals two consumer types, Wealth Preservers and Balanced Decumulators, that are indistinguishable by demographics but require fundamentally different product and communication strategies. Third, retirement experience increases the salience of wealth preservation in ways that workers without retirement experience fail to anticipate. Overall, our results suggest that coordination and product design, rather than fundamental conflicts of interest, constitute the primary bottleneck in decumulation markets.

detail.abstract: Purpose-This study aims to address a governance challenge emerging under mandatory sustainability and human rights due diligence regimes. As responsibility increasingly extends across interdependent value chain relationships, firms face growing pressure to integrate legally mandated sustainability obligations into the structures through which economic coordination and value creation are organized. The study examines how contractual governance can move beyond compliance and risk allocation to support both regulatory implementation and value creation. It develops the concept of shared value contracting to explain how contractual governance can integrate legally mandated responsibility and economic coordination across contemporary value chains. Design/methodology/approach-The research adopts a conceptual theory-building approach. It examines the governance implications of mandatory sustainability and human rights due diligence regimes and synthesizes insights from legal strategy, proactive contracting, contractual governance, shared value and sustainability governance scholarship. Through this synthesis, this study develops shared value contracting as a conceptual framework for understanding how contractual governance can integrate regulatory responsibility and economic coordination across interdependent value chain relationships.

detail.abstract: We examine whether the adoption of industrial automation technologies influences environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risk in an international setting. Using global industrial robotics data as a proxy for automation and ESG incident measures as a proxy for observed ESG risk, we find that robotics flow and stock are associated with higher firm-level ESG risk, including the frequency of ESG incidents, overall ESG risk index, and severity, reach, and novelty of these incidents. The effect is more pronounced for environmental and social incidents. Using fixed internet broadband subscriptions and population aging measures as instruments, we provide evidence consistent with a causal interpretation. We further provide evidence that firm-, industry-, and country-level factors can moderate this relationship. Our findings highlight an important yet often overlooked downside of automation—its potential to exacerbate ESG risks and impede corporate sustainability efforts. These results also underscore the importance of integrating ESG risk management into corporate technology transformation strategies.

title: Signals and Frictions: Which Luxury Strategies Survive AI Shopping Agents?
affiliations: Independent Researcher and Oklahoma State University

detail.title: Signals and Frictions: Which Luxury Strategies Survive AI Shopping Agents?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: AI shopping agents track prices, compare channels and countries, and complete purchases at almost no cost to their users. They therefore remove the frictions on which many pricing strategies rely. We ask which strategies of luxury brands survive. Our answer rests on a distinction between two sources of value. Some strategies draw their value from what observers infer about the owners of a good, and others draw it from frictions that buyers face. A faithful agent acts for the buyer, not for observers, so it removes the second source of value and leaves the first intact. We develop this idea in a model of a brand whose customers value the average type of the brand's other owners, and we obtain five results. First, a posted price is invariant to delegation and rises when AI helps observers recognize what others own. Second, for every form of discrimination in which discount buyers join the same clientele, such as markdowns, outlets, and private discounts, the brand's profit lies in a band that is the same for every shopping technology. The band narrows as status rises and closes at a threshold above which the brand never discounts. Third, regional price discrimination keeps the clienteles apart, so status gives it no protection, and agents erode it in the same proportion as for ordinary goods. Fourth, allocation of scarce goods through time, attention, or know-how collapses once agents make mimicry cheap, while allocation through required spending is immune to mimicry and is eroded only when AI makes the tied products easy to resell. Fifth, the one channel through which AI can erode signal-based strategies is delegation to agents that ignore status.

title: The Hidden Upside of Product Substitutability: Manufacturer Cost Asymmetry and Order Reallocation in Common-Retailer Supply Chains
affiliations: Georgia Southern University

detail.title: The Hidden Upside of Product Substitutability: Manufacturer Cost Asymmetry and Order Reallocation in Common-Retailer Supply Chains

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: Product substitutability is typically viewed as a destructive force in common-retailer supply chains: it intensifies manufacturer competition, compresses wholesale margins, and exacerbates within-assortment cannibalization. Yet firms routinely draw consumers' attention to product comparability. This tension motivates our analysis of how the profit consequences of substitutability change when the upstream supply base differs in production efficiency. We develop a common-retailer model in which cost-asymmetric manufacturers of horizontally substitutable products set wholesale prices before the retailer determines category-level order quantities. Cost asymmetry creates an efficiency-based order-reallocation mechanism absent from symmetric-manufacturer benchmarks: as products become closer substitutes, the retailer shifts order volume more aggressively toward lower-cost manufacturers. Stronger substitutability always harms high-cost manufacturers, but it can benefit lowcost manufacturers when the efficient cohort is sufficiently limited and its cost advantage sufficiently pronounced. It can also benefit the retailer far beyond the exceptionally small upstream networks permitted under manufacturer symmetry, provided the efficient cohort remains small and cost dispersion is sufficiently large. We then endogenize supply-base composition through manufacturers' cost-reducing investment decisions and show that diminishing returns to investment generate mixed-efficiency supply bases in equilibrium. These effects are nevertheless sensitive to channel governance. Under agency selling, the retailer-side upside disappears because the retailer loses the downstream allocation lever needed to monetize upstream cost differences. Under retailer margin commitment, the efficient-manufacturer upside survives and becomes easier to obtain, whereas the retailerside benefit contracts to a two-product assortment with sufficiently strong substitutability. Product substitutability is therefore not merely a margin-eroding force: when upstream efficiency is unevenly distributed and channel governance allows those differences to shape allocation, it can become a strategic asset.

title: Whom Should the Advisor Meet? Targeting Scarce Human Elicitation in AI-Enabled Financial

detail.abstract: AI-enabled advisory services raise an operating question about how human and automated work should be divided. Automated systems can handle customers at low marginal cost, whereas human advisors are more expensive and constrained by available time. A human can nevertheless add value when the customer information needed for the recommendation is difficult to obtain automatically. We examine this trade-off when the human advantage is concentrated in preference elicitation rather than in portfolio optimization. We represent the advisory encounter as two connected stages. The first stage obtains information about a customer's private preference; the second uses that information to generate a recommendation. A customer-level measure, the net marginal value of human elicitation, links three decisions: whether to involve a human, which customers should receive human service when capacity is limited, and how much advisory capacity to provide. The measure reflects the improvement in information, the responsiveness of the downstream decision, the economic consequences of decision error, and the cost of human service. Using 19,022 respondents from the 2024 National Financial Capability Study, we estimate heterogeneous priors for investment risk tolerance and use them in the service-system model. The information and cost parameters that cannot be identified from the survey are calibrated. Under the baseline calibration, human-assisted elicitation is preferred for 37.65% of customers when capacity is unconstrained. With capacity fixed at 20% of the sample, the value-index policy produces $141,093 in aggregate net welfare relative to AI-only service, compared with $128,283 for wealth-based routing, $88,227 for complexity-based routing, and-$36,063 for uncertainty-based routing. The comparison indicates that the value of human involvement depends on how information changes the downstream decision, rather than on uncertainty or another customer characteristic taken by itself.

detail.abstract: The United States and China have agreed to a bilateral AI dialogue and an incident communication channel, with the next round expected in November. In the same fortnight, OpenAI cancelled GPT-6.1 Astra after it failed an internal safety bar, Anthropic warned investors that autonomous agents create unpredictable legal exposure, and NVIDIA shipped a runtime platform for constraining agents out of band. This paper argues that AI safety must now be judged at three levels at once — government commitments, laboratory release discipline, and technical enforcement in deployment — and proposes six public tests that distinguish an operating oversight regime from a declaration. It closes with four stress scenarios that show why the layers must meet, and a standard of evidence an ordinary observer could verify without classified access.

detail.abstract: This study aims to investigate How does the automation-augmentation paradox affect PSO in navigating their Gen AI transformation? To answer this research question, we develop a case study using an action research method (Coughlan & Coghlan, 2002) over a twenty-month time period, working with Dublin City Council, a local authority in the Republic of Ireland. The findings of this study show that the Gen AI transformation in PSOs is hindered by pre-existing and unsolvable epistemic, organisational, and institutional challenges. Instead of focusing on the challenges mentioned above, PSOs could focus on concrete and actionable problems these challenges create to achieve successful Gen AI transformation. Besides that, from the automation-augmentation paradox theory perspective, we found that the augmentation-automation relationship is the mechanism that explains why problems PSOs face hinder their successful Gen AI transformation and why actions proposed in this study are effective.

detail.abstract: This paper 1 provides a comprehensive assessment of the Government of India's Digital India initiative and attempts to evaluate its potential to generate transformative socioeconomic and governance outcomes, particularly for India's 900 million plus rural inhabitants. Building upon an earlier TPRC53 paper 2 , this study draws exclusively on publicly available information from government, industry, and civil-society sources to provide an updated, evidence-based examination of Digital India's progress, achievements, and persistent challenges. The analysis situates the initiative within India's historically entrenched rural-urban disparities in infrastructure-most notably in electricity, transportation, and communications-and explores the extent to which digital interventions may help to reduce these structural inequalities. Overall, the paper provides a critical appraisal of Digital India's achievements to date, while identifying the remaining barriers that must be addressed for the initiative to fulfill its transformative potential. By analyzing both achievements and continuing challenges, this paper provides an evidence-based evaluation of whether the "elephant" of India's large and complex governance system can indeed "dance"-and what that would mean for the country's socioeconomic transformation.

detail.abstract: Drug discovery of new therapeutics, although critical to human health, is an inherently long and resource-intensive process that tends to rely on high-throughput screening and computational methods, such as Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship (QSAR) modeling. Nevertheless, both QSAR and high-throughput screening fall short in their ability to move quickly and Offer uniqueness. This paper presents an approach that is powered by reinforcement learning (RL) and a multi-layer perceptron neural network called deep Q-network (DQN) for accelerated identification and, ultimately, optimization of new drug candidates. By utilizing Al-based algorithms, our approach is capable of operating in vast chemical spaces, producing new molecular structures, and optimizing various attributes, such as potency, selectivity, and drug-likeness, all at the same time. The RL agent is trained with a dynamic reward function, balancing competing objectives such as maximizing binding affinity while minimizing toxicity. Our results show that the approach outlined in this paper outperforms conventional methods, yielding an accuracy of 91.2% in molecular property predictions and a 40% increase in the novelty of molecules compared to both traditional QSAR and high-throughput screening methods and conventional chemists. Furthermore, the output of this model can produce new drug-like molecules in less than five minutes per iteration, laying a novel approach to accelerating drug discovery, the optimization of molecular attributes, and neglected diseases.

detail.abstract: A local-volatility surface must reprice the vanilla grid under the finite-difference engine that values the book. Analytic Dupire surfaces frequently fail this round-trip test: on our SPX sample calibrated eSSVI surfaces misprice by 30 bp of implied volatility on a root-mean-square basis. The industry standard approach is to calibrate the surface numerically as in Andreasen and Huge (2011). This passes the round trip by construction if the surface fits the market but tends to produce a rough surface and unstable sensitivities. Numerical calibration can also be slow and with the typically large number of parameters may not converge to a global optimum. This paper develops an alternative approach that keeps the base surface and removes the residual with derivative-free bootstrap iterations forward over quoted maturities. The local-volatility slice for each time interval or tenor is scaled by a smoothed power of the ratio of market to model implied volatility, with the exponent updated by a secant regression on successive errors. No Jacobian of the pricing map is calculated; one pricing per sweep replaces the one-pricing-per-node of a derivative-based numerical optimization. This can be thought of as a smooth correction to the base surface, and the method is agnostic to the surface it corrects. We demonstrate it on two calibrated surfaces: the analytic Dupire surfaces derived from a Hendriks-Martini eSSVI fit, and the previous day's numerically calibrated surfaces re-interpolated onto today's strikes. Accuracy is benchmarked against a full Andreasen-Huge (AH) calibration. The data consist of daily SPX vol surfaces for the period from 22 June 2023 to 30 April 2026 (714 surfaces). All pricing is done by backward PDE in Numerix CrossAsset. With eSSVI as the base the pooled round-trip RMSE is 3.47 bp on volatility. Iterating from the previous day's surface (warm start) gives 3.88 bp against 3.34 bp for full AH calibrations. Uncorrected eSSVI and warm start return 30 bp and 67 bp respectively. At maturities out to two years, where most of the book's Vega sits, the correction is more accurate than the full calibration: 2.12 and 2.08 bp out to one year against 3.07 bp, and 2.55 and 2.64 bp out to two years against 3.02 bp. The corrected surface outperforms the benchmark on 68 percent of market days out to two years. Beyond two years the benchmark is more accurate, 5.05 bp against 7.11 bp. There the quotes are sparse, noisy and a year apart, a coarse spline cannot follow noisy strike structure, and in a bootstrap the long columns can only absorb what the already-fitted short slices leave them; the iteration reaches its projected fixed point and is limited by representation, not convergence. The stopping criteria are anchored to the benchmark's per-expiry empirical accuracy-its median slice error is 1.01 bp and its median maximum deviation 4.11 bp. detail.abstract: Public policy analysis is often presented as a technical exercise in gathering information, comparing alternatives and recommending action. In practice, it is also an ethical and political activity: analysts decide how a problem is framed, whose knowledge is recognised, which outcomes count as success and how costs and benefits are distributed. This conceptual review brings together three connected dimensions of policy analysis: methodological choice, the influence of think tanks, and the intellectual and social skills required of policy analysts. It examines interviews, documentary analysis and observation; interpretive approaches such as framing, narrative, storytelling and dramaturgical analysis; quantitative techniques including descriptive statistics, time-series, factor and path analysis; and qualitative approaches such as case study, ethnography and action research. It then considers consequentialist, deontological and virtue-ethical reasoning, before examining how think tanks generate ideas, supply expertise, educate citizens, convene debate and connect research with government. The article argues that neither rigorous data nor expert advice is sufficient on its own. Effective policy analysis depends on the integration of credible evidence, transparent value judgments, implementation awareness, independent knowledge institutions and meaningful public participation. Illustrations drawn from Zimbabwe and wider African policy contexts show why technical competence must be matched by attention to local knowledge, equity, cultural diversity and accountability. The article offers an integrated framework for evidence-informed, ethical and inclusive policy analysis.

detail.abstract: A text model can sit next to a live trading system the way a thermometer sits next to a patient: it reads, it never prescribes. We follow one such model into a lab running an intraday strategy and a second, overnight strategy on one account. It is a small commercial judge, pinned to one version, that answers only typed questions about headlines. We describe six tests for a text signal: read a plain fact correctly against a real label, beat a simple count of its own headlines, show no memory of famous past events, give the same answer twice, always see the decision-time date, and check each forward verdict rule against random flags. They were assembled over three days, most of them after a failure, and we present them as the checklist we would now apply up front. We compare the judge with a general chatbot on blind rows, list what it may touch (stamps written after the close, counted forward) and what it may never touch (any number in the trading system), and report the plumbing failures that corrupted its readings. Its readings so far are small: one fact read well, one small effect below its bar, several that vanished; the fact was read under one setup, and its margin over a simple headline count is borderline. None of the six tests is new on its own; what is new is using them together on a text instrument beside a live system, and reporting every study it was used in, failures included. This is a paper about checking data and the instrument, not about profit: we make no claim about either strategy's returns.

detail.abstract: Between 2013 and 2022, the Israeli central government signed bilateral Umbrella Agreements with 37 municipalities, committing to the construction of 462,984 dwelling units to alleviate a national housing affordability crisis. While critical planning literature hypothesized that these centralized development pacts would induce municipal fiscal distress and widen spatial inequality, the realized long-term local impacts have remained empirically unexamined. Utilizing an administrative panel of 268 local authorities spanning 2000 to 2024, we evaluate the program through a continuous-dose event-study design with municipality-level block bootstrapping. Our estimates exclude adverse fiscal dislocations, demonstrating that signatory municipalities maintained stable budgetary equilibria. Specifically, the empirical results rule out post-signing increases in intergovernmental transfer dependency exceeding 2.5 percentage points, and reject erosions in the non-residential property tax share larger than 7.4 percentage points, with formal equivalence tests confirming stability across pre-specified policy bounds. For housing transaction prices, the achieved equivalence bound of 7.5% excludes large market disruptions, although the empirical design lacks the statistical resolution to detect the modest price dampening documented in localized micro-supply literature. We demonstrate that this pervasive local stability was driven by a severe implementation deficit: state audits show that actual land marketing achieved only 33% of the contractual residential pace and 7% of commercial allocations, leaving the physical mechanisms of municipal fiscal dilution largely unactivated.

detail.abstract: How does perceived relative income affect household behavior and well-being? We use a randomized information experiment in a representative panel of Dutch households to generate exogenous variation in beliefs about peers' income. Lower perceived relative standing shifts expenditure toward durable goods but we find little evidence of an increase in total spending. Higher perceived relative income increases socializing and substantially raises happiness, while lower relative income increases subsequent employment. Relative standing also shapes views about inequality and redistribution. A complementary vignette experiment provides supporting evidence on mechanisms. Overall, peer comparisons matter for behavior and well-being even when total spending responses are small.

detail.abstract: We present a methodology for generating uncertainty indicators for user-defined topics based on newspaper data. The approach is based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems commonly used in artificial intelligence applications, which we adapt to construct topic-specific uncertainty measures, referred to as Retrieval-Augmented Uncertainty Indicators (RAUI). The method employs semantic search with an embedding model to select news articles relevant to a given topic, and a large language model (LLM) to quantify the level of uncertainty contained in each of those articles. We construct uncertainty indicators for ten topics using Spanish newspaper data and an aggregate measure that also highlights how each topic contributes to overall uncertainty. We present two practical applications of these indicators: a VAR analysis that shows how different sources of uncertainty have different effects on the Spanish economy, and an estimation that generates time-varying fan charts around the Banco de España GDP growth projections.

detail.abstract: This paper estimates the effects of standard monetary policy shocks on housing and other macro variables in Slovakia, a CESEE country. For that purpose, we use a non-linear local projection model which uncovers asymmetries in these effects around three different dimensions: high versus low economic growth, interest rates and inflation. The main findings in this study are as follows. First, we often find no evidence of standard monetary policy eliciting a contractionary response in house prices or housing investment. Second, evidence is weakest during recessions and periods of low interest rates or low inflation. Third, these findings may be linked to the inability of monetary policy to trigger significant contractionary effects on household lending, which in turn may be linked to the effective lower bound on interest rates, the predominance of fixed-rate mortgages in Slovakia or interaction between monetary and macroprudential policy. We also discuss the possible country characteristics that might drive these results and policy implications.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the deposit channel of monetary policy during the fastest and most intense tightening cycle of the euro era. Using the Banco de España’s Central Credit Register and regional variation in deposit market concentration, we show that the limited pass-through of policy rates to deposit rates produces heterogeneous effects on bank credit supply and risk-taking. Following the tightening cycle, banks operating in more concentrated deposit markets reduced credit more sharply to riskier firms. For newly originated loans, this contraction was accompanied by higher interest rates and improved realized returns. We document a novel dimension of the deposit channel: it compels banks to actively optimize their risk-return trade-off. Our results show that preserving deposit franchise value leads banks to prioritize prudence, reversing the “search-for-yield” dynamic observed during the zero-lower-bound era.

detail.abstract: Statistical tests reject the expectations hypothesis (EH) even at the very short end of the term structure, yet trading on the rejections earns little. Because these tests assume a linear model of expectations, it has remained open whether a less restrictive test would uncover economically meaningful departures. We test an implication of the EH that holds for any expectations process, namely that the excess return of rolling over short repos instead of holding a longer repo is unpredictable. The test is out of sample, on daily US generalcollateral repo rates from overnight to one month over 1998-2026, with linear, tree-based, and neural-network forecasts estimated under one protocol. The in-sample Wald test rejects a true EH in 88% to 97% of simulated samples and is therefore uninformative. Out of sample, departures are predictable only at horizons of one and two weeks, a linear function of current rates captures them, and most of this predictability disappears when same-day composite quotes are excluded. Relaxing the functional form does not change the economic conclusion: trading on any of 22 forecasts earns at most 2.2 basis points a year before costs and 0.9 after observed bid-ask spreads, and even perfect foresight of the excess return would earn at most 4.1 basis points a year per unit of notional before costs. Statistical rejections of the EH at the short end thus coexist with a tight economic bound on its failure.

detail.abstract: We study what two candidate-generation procedures recover from a fixed corpus of Kalshi and Polymarket contract representations. Thirty days of collection yield 1,029,600 Kalshi market records and 1,226 Polymarket market identifiers under 100 observed parent events. A lexical procedure reports 3,117,473 candidate pairs. A field-aware procedure produces 1,486,341 verified relation rows across 75 nonempty parent anchors. Every parent count equals the Cartesian product of its Polymarket children and Kalshi subject hits; a single Bitcoin block contributes 78.77 percent of the relation. A fixed, hash-ranked sample of 294 pairs is then examined using full captured terms. Eighty-eight records retain unresolved literal child-identity labels. The remaining 206 receive documentary annotations of differences in their recorded propositions, including event occurrence versus utterance, winning versus reaching a vote-share threshold, and path barriers versus fixed-time measurements. The results quantify candidate expansion and document failure mechanisms in the executed retrieval procedures. They do not estimate venue-wide contract equivalence or the accuracy of an independently validated matching system.

detail.abstract: We examine how recorded event-contract terms select data vintages and the granularity of observations required for payout evaluation. The study uses a thirty-day Kalshi corpus containing 1,029,600 distinct market representations and 6,842,078 lifecycle message associations. An enumeration of 931 contracts naming Carbon Arc identifies 248 first-reported-value clauses and 683 finalized-value clauses with explicit calendar cutoffs. A bounded sports case study decodes preserved source pages and links one reported full-game score to a family of 264 contracts. Conditional on the same completed game, applicable rules and normal settlement branch, that score evaluates 78 full-game numerical predicates, but does not identify a selected third-quarter predicate. A separate field-path census finds numerical determination and settlement timestamps in every corresponding message association, although a top-level sending timestamp is present in only 10.83 percent of all associations. The findings document distinct sources of measurement error: selecting the wrong data vintage, using observations at the wrong aggregation level, and treating one missing timestamp field as absence of all temporal information. The study reports corpus-level descriptions and bounded contract-level calculations, not the time at which public evidence first became contractually decisive.

detail.abstract: Political costs have long been invoked as a significant friction that constrains firms' tax avoidance behavior. However, empirical findings are mixed and provide virtually no evidence of politicians' perceptions of and responses to tax avoidance. We extend the political cost literature by conducting a survey and field experiment with state legislators. Our results shed light on the types of firm behaviors that may cause legislators to take action, the actions legislators might take, and legislators' views on appropriate tax rates, corporate tax incidence, and preferred sources of tax revenue. On most issues we find large, significant differences between Democrats and Republicans. However, both sides view legal tax avoidance as less important than illegal tax evasion, even when avoidance results in a low effective tax rate. Our findings guide future archival research by identifying conditions under which political costs are more likely to constrain firms' tax avoidance.

detail.abstract: Retail banking relationships have historically been protected less by price than by the effort required to switch, researching alternatives, opening accounts, moving direct deposits, closing the old relationship. This effort based protection is referred to as a "switching cost moat." This paper investigates how agentic artificial intelligence, exemplified by Meta's Muse, launched September 8, 2026, which can compare deposit rates and execute financial transactions through a Plaid integration spanning over 12,000 institutions, may fill that moat by driving the effort cost of switching toward zero, independent of any change in the underlying rate incentive itself. This paper constructed the first rigorous, regulatory data grounded empirical baseline of how much this effort cost has historically suppressed rate driven deposit switching, using Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council (FFIEC) data for a selected bank sample (2006-2026) and National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) data for credit unions (2006-2021). This research found a real, statistically significant, but modest and continuous (not threshold) relationship, roughly 0.40 to 0.66 percentage points of deposit share migration per percentage point of rate spread, explaining at most 19-70% of quarterly variation depending on sample and sub-period. This baseline is situated against the 2013 launch of Yu'e Bao in China, in which one-click switching from payment app balances into a money market fund produced the fastest mutual fund growth ever recorded, and against mortgage lending, where borrowers already demonstrably pay a premium for reduced friction. Together, this evidence suggests the historical weakness of rate driven switching has been substantially an effort cost phenomenon, not a price awareness one, and that agentic AI, by construction, targets exactly that effort cost.

detail.abstract: The article reviews the Situation in the State of Palestine (ICC-01/18) before the International Criminal Court, from the article 12(3) declaration and accession of January 2015 to the developments of 2025-2026. Drawing on V. Ageyev's historical and terminological studies, it distinguishes 'Palestine' as a toponym, the Palestinian people as the holder of the right to selfdetermination, and the 'State of Palestine' as the entity that seized the Court. It argues that the 2015 acts which triggered the Court's jurisdiction were performed by an entity whose statehood under general international law was unconfirmed at the critical date, and that the Court never examined that question on the merits. Separately, and irrespective of the statehood dispute, it shows that in January 2015 the applicant exercised no governmental authority in the Gaza Strip, to which the 2024 warrants relate. The procedural flaws identified include the use of article 19(3) at the situation stage; the deferral and later dismissal as premature of the Oslo Accords argument, which the Appeals Chamber found on 24 April 2025 to be an error of law; the narrowing of article 18; the public announcement of warrant applications; and the undecided request to disqualify the Prosecutor. The conduct of the Prosecutor and the judges is tested against the OTP policy papers, the Chambers Practice Manual and the codes of ethics. United States sanctions against the Court's judges and prosecutors are assessed as incompatible with judicial independence and as lacking a legitimate aim, since the Statute itself provides the proper avenue of challenge. The article also traces the fragmentation of support among European States Parties and shows how the designation of Hamas as a terrorist organization relates to the allegations brought before the Court. It concludes with proposals on the protection of victims and suspects and with scenarios for the proceedings, including their bearing on the Situation in Ukraine (ICC-01/22).

detail.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) accounts for 59% of global textile fiber production, and its synthesis relies on antimony catalysts, a suspected human carcinogen. The enzyme Candida antarctica Lipase B (CALB) catalyzes polyester synthesis without leaving a metal residue and with more mild reaction conditions. Though there is no data on using CALB for PET specifically, it is used as a proxy here for a prospective enzymatic route. Cost is frequently cited as the barrier to adoption in general, and this paper tests that claim by deriving catalyst and energy costs for both catalysts from commodity price data and reaction stoichiometry, then applying Wright's law to determine whether learning effects in the enzyme production close the gap. Findings resulted in an enzymatic cost of $931.85 per ton against $17.62 for antimony, meaning that parity is reached only under the most optimistic learning rate scenario at ~2% of global PET output. The Jacobian sensitivity matrix confirmed the parity's sensitivity to the learning rate. The Monte Carlo simulation across 10,000 draws places the probability of parity within global production at 50.4%. The threshold analysis revealed that the binding constraint is catalyst efficiency rather than production scale.

detail.abstract: We investigate whether improved financial scenario coverage transfers to useful decisions when neural feature models, local language-model selectors and reporting components are combined. The framework separates seven-class S&P 500 price-path scenarios, KOSPI action choices, numerical comprehension and realized-policy evaluation. On previously inspected historical data, the recorded B3 system achieves Top-2 coverage of 50.81% and 55.95% at the five- and twenty-session horizons. A matched-budget component study supports a five-session contribution from the pair-selection head, while rare-case failures remain substantial. Feedback-driven analyses control training budget, transaction costs, realized exposure and market inputs, and examine calibration and utility sensitivity. Multi-task factual improvements do not automatically establish better financial choices or incremental timing value. Task-specific decision heads and gradient-conflict adjustment are evaluated separately from the earlier single-head continuation, with all scheduled seeds retained rather than selecting the best test run. The additional three-seed cross-entropy continuation reduced retrospective action accuracy from 54.63% to 51.98%, despite a development improvement; report and stock numerical-choice accuracy increased by 1.04 and 2.08 percentage points. The evidence supports an auditable, locally executed framework for separating classification, comprehension and economic claims, but not a general claim of profitable timing or prospective superiority. The historical evaluation has been reused, market-source limitations remain, and prospective outcomes are pending.

title: Quantifying Distance-Dependent Measurement Errors in Vehicular Trajectory Data Collection
affiliations: Northwestern University, University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign, University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign, Northwestern University, University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and Northwestern University

detail.title: Quantifying Distance-Dependent Measurement Errors in Vehicular Trajectory Data Collection

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no potential conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract:
Objectives: Trajectory datasets collected by the onboard sensors of automated vehicles (AVs) are an increasingly common resource for traffic research. Unlike infrastructure-based sensors, an AV observes surrounding vehicles from a continuously changing vantage point, so the accuracy of a measurement depends on how far away its target is. This study asks whether such distance-dependent errors are consequential for downstream traffic analyses.

Methods: We develop a general, sensor-agnostic error model that separates two sources of uncertainty conflated in AV-based sensing---the vehicle's error in locating itself and its error in ranging to a target---and represents distance-dependent bias, distance-dependent noise, and temporal correlation in each. We calibrate the model through a controlled two-vehicle field experiment with GPS and radar, then inject the resulting error structure, together with a broader family of hypothetical structures, into the Third Generation Simulation (TGSIM) I-90/94 dataset treated as a proxy for ground truth. Comparing analyses of the error-injected trajectories against the proxy isolates the effect of measurement error on static properties (gap sizes), macroscopic relationships (speed-density-flow), and trajectory-level metrics (speed variance and headway).

Findings: Distance-dependent bias displaces gap measurements with or without AV involvement by different amounts, because the two are reconstructed from different combinations of range observations. Under the empirically calibrated error structure, this displacement is sufficient to reverse a statistical conclusion: measured data may indicate that human drivers follow AVs more closely than they follow other human-driven vehicles (HVs), which the ground-truth trajectories do not support. At the macroscopic level, bias produces regime-dependent distortions in flow and density that propagate into capacity assessment. At the trajectory level, it introduces location-dependent biases in speed variance and average headway, so that a vehicle's observed driving behavior depends in part on where it sat relative to the sensor. Unbiased distance-dependent uncertainty is largely attenuated by trajectory smoothing, though it still biases speed variance, since smoothing effectiveness itself varies with the local noise magnitude.

Novelty: This study is among the first to systematically quantify how distance-dependent sensor error structures in AV-collected trajectory data bias traffic analysis at both microscopic and macroscopic levels, and to separate the consequences of systematic bias from those of random uncertainty---a distinction that matters because aggregation removes the latter but not the former.

Practical Applications: The findings highlight the importance of reporting distance-specific sensor error characteristics, rather than just aggregate accuracy measures, when collecting, processing, and analyzing AV-collected trajectory datasets. Our framework also provides practical guidance for trajectory data quality assessment.

detail.abstract: Children in immigrant families often interpret speech, explain documents, complete forms, and mediate encounters between adults and public institutions. This work can express competence, care, and family solidarity. It can also expose a child to confidential information, adult conflict, technical decisions, and responsibility for consequences that the child cannot control. Research has documented both sides of this practice, yet institutional analysis often treats child language brokering as a private family arrangement. This article reframes it as a public-service design issue. It uses a structured qualitative review of 35 scholarly, legal, and professional sources available by 15 September 2026. The analysis covers education, health care, administrative services, family relations, and developmental outcomes in the United States. The article develops the Child Language Brokering Safeguard Framework. The framework applies six tests: institutional necessity, stakes and suitability, voluntariness and capacity, privacy and emotional exposure, role boundaries, and adult verification. It distinguishes ordinary family help from institutional substitution. The distinction matters because a child may choose to explain a routine message at home, while a hospital, school, court, or benefits office may still have a duty to provide competent adult language assistance. The article argues that institutions should not measure success by whether communication was completed. They should ask who carried the burden, what risks were transferred, whether the child could refuse, and whether an accountable adult verified the result. Children's bilingual abilities should be recognized without converting them into unpaid infrastructure. Public services can respect family agency while preserving adult responsibility, confidentiality, and meaningful access.

detail.abstract: Decision making is a fundamental activity in organizational management that is influenced by the level of information availability and the characteristics of the environment in which the decision is made. This conceptual research aims to comprehensively analyze the typology of the decision environment which includes conditions of certainty, risk, uncertainty, conflict, and ever-changing environmental dynamics. The analysis method is carried out in a qualitative descriptive manner through the review of the theoretical literature and the exploration of the empirical case of the merger of Gojek and Tokopedia (GoTo). The results of the discussion show that the success of the decision is highly dependent on the suitability between the type of environment and the quantitative and qualitative methods applied. The certainty condition is solved by deterministic maximization; the risk condition relies on probability criteria such as Expected Value (EV) and Expected Opportunity Loss (EOL); the uncertainty condition requires non-probabilistic criteria (Maximax, Maximin, Laplace, Minimax Regret, Hurwicz); while the conflict condition is solved through Game Theory. Modern decision-makers are required to have strategic flexibility in responding to consecutive feedback in a dynamic environment.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of data centers is creating large, geographically concentrated increases in electricity demand. Rising demand has shaped public opinion around fears of rising electricity prices and led to numerous bans on AI data center development in the US. In this paper, we empirically study how data center entry affects electricity prices. We link quarterly data center capacity additions data with local electricity price and utility sales data, and implement a single-anchor synthetic-control design with cumulative, repeated treatment to estimate the causal effect of data center growth on retail electricity prices. We find that the additional data centers built in the US between 2020 and 2025 increased their region's industrial electricity price by an average of 5.4 $/MWh, explaining 15% of the total observed increase in prices. Furthermore, we show that there are significant but small spillovers to residential consumers, increasing prices by an average of 1.7 $/MWh, which accounts for 4% of the observed increase since 2020. We then analyze which factors explain differences in price impacts and find that data center additions by Big Tech firms result in no discernible price increases, whereas co-location data centers do. Also, counterintuitively, utilities with previously higher infrastructure utilization and a history of serving large industrial customers have lower residential spillovers. Overall, our findings suggest that the prevailing discourse about data centers affecting electricity affordability is overstated, and that the average residential price effect is small and concentrated among co-location developers and specific utilities.

detail.abstract:
Organizations increasingly deploy artificial intelligence while struggling to convert experimentation into
durable economic value. Recent practitioner evidence suggests that firms generating greater AI value
combine strategic clarity with applied AI capability, but that observation does not by itself specify the
organizational mechanism through which capability becomes financial performance. This paper proposes
the Directed Agency Value Model (DAVM), a conceptual framework in which agentic AI value depends on
three complementary organizational capacities: Strategic Clarity, Agentic Capability, and Operational
Conversion. Strategic Clarity concerns where AI should be deployed and how opportunities are prioritized
and owned. Agentic Capability concerns the ability to delegate bounded decisions and actions to AI while
maintaining verification, auditability, and reversibility. Operational Conversion concerns the
transformation of AI use cases into redesigned workflows that operate at scale and generate attributable
economic effects. The paper introduces two additional constructs. Clarity Debt measures the share of AI
investment lacking adequate ownership, baseline measurement, or financial accountability. Verified
Autonomy defines effective agency as the portion of granted autonomy that can be supported by
demonstrated verification capacity. A Cobb–Douglas-type functional form is proposed as a testable
representation of complementarity, but its parameters are not estimated in the present paper. The paper
develops propositions concerning complementarity, conversion, Clarity Debt, and verification constraints;
proposes a 40-indicator measurement instrument organized around the three pillars; and specifies an
empirical validation program designed to compare DAVM against additive and bottleneck alternatives. The
contribution is therefore theoretical and methodological: DAVM offers an open framework for studying how
organizational direction, agency, and workflow transformation jointly condition the economic value of
agentic AI.

detail.abstract: Studies of US adults up to 2019 mostly found the gap in psychological distress between socioeconomic groups widening. For the years since, official statistics give figures by income for single years, and one federal report found symptoms of anxiety and depression rising between 2019 and 2022 in every income group except the poorest. This paper measures how the gap in distress between income groups changed from 2014 to 2024, and tests whether a change in a person's income is followed by a change in their distress. It uses 176,781 person-years from adults in the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, with distress measured on the Kessler-6 (K6) scale, and follows 43,954 adults over two consecutive years with fixed-effects models. Serious distress rose from 3.7% in 2014-2019 to 4.7% in 2022-2024, but the difference between the poorest and richest income groups did not change (7.6 and 7.4 percentage points; p = 0.79), with or without education, marital status and other characteristics held constant. In exploratory analyses by severity, the gap narrowed at milder levels: from 19.2 to 14.4 percentage points for moderate or worse distress (p < 0.001), and to close to zero for reporting any symptoms. The rise in serious distress was concentrated among adults under 45. Within the same person, a change of income group was not followed by a change in distress over one year, whereas becoming unable to work was. Milder distress spread to better-off and younger adults, while the burden of serious distress among the poor did not fall.

detail.abstract: AWS Glue's memory-optimized R-series workers, introduced alongside larger G-series workers in July 2025, promise double the memory of a standard Data Processing Unit (DPU) for Spark ETL workloads that are memory-rather than compute-bound. This paper examines what can be rigorously benchmarked about this comparison using only officially published data, and is explicit about a gap this creates: no publicly available, controlled runtime benchmark comparing AWS Glue's G-series and R-series workers exists as of this paper's preparation, since the R-series is too recent for such a study to have emerged in the public record. In its place, we establish a genuine, AWS-confirmed quantitative finding at the configuration level: for G.1X and G.2X workers, AWS's own troubleshooting documentation shows spark.executor.memory is set to approximately 62.5% of each worker's nominal DPU memory (10 GB of 16 GB for G.1X; 20 GB of 32 GB for G.2X), meaning nearly 40% of a worker's advertised memory is unavailable to Spark tasks and reserved for YARN, OS, and off-heap overhead. We show this ratio is identical across both measured G-series sizes, and, while AWS has not published the equivalent figure for the R-series, we present the hypothesis that the same ratio would yield approximately 20 GB of usable executor memory for R.1X against its 32 GB nominal allocation-a hypothesis we label explicitly as this paper's own extrapolation, not an AWS-confirmed figure. We situate this finding within AWS's officially documented OOM error taxonomy and Amazon EMR's published guidance on memory-optimized instance selection, and propose a concrete benchmarking methodology, including the specific measurements needed to confirm or refute this paper's central hypothesis, for the controlled study we argue is still missing from the public record.

detail.abstract: We theoretically and experimentally study procurement auctions for infrastructure projects with post-auction risk. We compare fixed-payment (cash) auctions, scaling (unit-price) auctions, and a novel cost-sharing auction in which bidders compete by requesting a fraction of variable costs to be covered. Our experiments vary how bidder heterogeneity enters the environment: through input-quantity risk or through marginal costs. We find that scaling auctions can outperform fixed-payment auctions when heterogeneity operates through marginal costs but perform poorly when heterogeneity operates through quantity risk. Our theoretical analysis of cost-sharing auctions demonstrates how they can combine efficient allocation with risk sharing. Our results provide experimental evidence on the trade-off between risk sharing and adverse selection in procurement design.

detail.abstract: This paper examines patterns of land-use regulatory change in Santiago, Chile, focusing on downzoning (stricter regulations) and upzoning (more flexible regulations), and its associations with socio-demographic factors. We analyze an original georeferenced dataset covering all 34 urban municipalities of Santiago over 20 years, together with 19 semi-structured interviews with key actors. The quantitative analysis suggests that high-income neighborhoods are associated with a greater likelihood of downzoning when homeownership is comparatively low. With our block-level measure of wealth, however, this association is not statistically distinguishable from zero at the sample average homeownership rate and becomes negative at higher rates. Therefore, in affluent neighborhoods the significant presence of homeowners is associated with less probability of downzoning. Outside highincome neighborhoods, higher homeownership is instead associated with downzoning. Qualitative evidence points to the growing role of organized residents, with socially connected groups using participatory reforms and informal ties to municipal decision-makers to shape local regulatory debates. This positive association is absent when the analysis is restricted to large-scale zoning changes. The findings contribute to debates between the "growth machine" and "homevoter" theories by suggesting that the relevance of each framework may vary across patterns of social segmentation and local demographic structures.

detail.abstract: This paper maps language-of-instruction achievement gaps across the post-Soviet space. We harmonize student-level microdata from PISA, TIMSS, and PIRLS for thirteen successor states between 1999 and 2025, covering roughly 720,000 students in 26,000 schools, and estimate the gap between students taught in Russian and in the national (titular) language. Four patterns emerge. First, the gap's sign is regionally patterned: by age 15 it favours titular-language students in the Baltics and Russian-language students in Central Asia and Azerbaijan. Second, where gaps exist they range from a tenth to a full standard deviation and, though narrowing in places, have persisted across a quarter-century of de-Russification. Recent narrowing is mostly convergence through decline, the historically advantaged stream falling faster after 2018. Third, the gap widens or narrows as cohorts progress through school, suggesting that schooling itself may reproduce or erode linguistic stratification. Fourth, socioeconomic status predicts the gaps only where the streams differ in socioeconomic composition, and not always there. It explains about half of Azerbaijan's gap and almost none of Kazakhstan's, whose reading gap of 0.9 standard deviations survives every socioeconomic control. The findings recast the Soviet legacy of dual language-of-instruction schooling as a contested axis of inequality.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) expands financial prediction and information processing, but technical gains do not necessarily improve allocation. This theory-guided survey synthesizes 209 publications through information economics, constrained choice, delegation, and strategic feedback. We trace tool evolution and distinguish measurement, historical policy evaluation, observed adoption, and equilibrium mechanisms. Three conclusions organize the evidence. First, prediction gains create net value only through feasible actions after implementation costs. Second, more precise signals can improve selection while either expanding or contracting funding; contracts and capacity determine the allocation response. Third, human discretion and counterparty adaptation make deployed performance endogenous. A Gaussian benchmark and five conditional propositions explain these distinctions without claiming a new unified equilibrium. The literature supports task-specific information gains, heterogeneous credit-pricing counterfactuals, and issuer adaptation, while sustained deployment value, competitive rent erosion, and aggregate welfare remain less securely established. The synthesis identifies the assumptions behind apparently conflicting findings and prioritizes empirical designs that observe thresholds, rival access, recommendations, and executed decisions.

detail.abstract: We study whether lowering the cost of accessing mandatory corporate disclosures enhances financial market quality. We exploit the SEC's staggered introduction of EDGAR, whose rollout-wave assignments were randomized conditional on firm size and thus supplies plausibly exogenous variation in the timing of firms' shift to electronic filing. We carefully separate administrative filing dates from the moments investors could actually retrieve the filings, incorporating both the launch of free public access and firms' reporting cycles. Our research design begins with the economic quantity of interest, defines the comparisons that identify it, and then applies a staggered differencein-differences estimator. We find gains in market quality: liquidity rises by roughly 7 percent, bid-ask spreads fall by approximately 10 percent, and idiosyncratic volatility declines. Because EDGAR left disclosure requirements unchanged and merely reduced the frictions of obtaining the information, the results offer causal evidence that lower information-dissemination costs can substantially improve market functioning.

detail.abstract:
I develop a framework linking pretrend tests, preperiod selection, and estimation in difference-indifferences. Under one maintained parallel-trends restriction, pretrend restrictions are equivalent to additional restrictions identifying the same treatment effect. Within extended two-way fixed effects, the pretrend Wald statistic equals the corresponding GMM J statistic under compatible covariance construction. This equivalence makes established moment-selection procedures implementable from familiar event-study output. I develop Wald-BIC selection of valid restrictions and focused selection balancing local bias and variance. Rejection over an extended preperiod window need not invalidate a design justified over a shorter window.
