detail.abstract: Twenty-five years after the United Nations Security Council adopted Resolution 1325 on Women, Peace and Security (WPS), Nigeria has produced three National Action Plans to put it into practice: in 2013, 2017 and, most recently, for 2024-2028. Yet in the conflict-affected North, where women have borne heavy costs from insurgency, banditry and communal violence, the framework's promise of women's participation in peace and security remains distant. This article asks why a global framework written in New York struggles to reach women in places such as Maiduguri. Drawing on the Mamman's research on how international agencies treat social knowledge, on recent work on civic belonging in divided democracies, and on feminist scholarship on WPS, it identifies three gaps. The first is a knowledge gap: the framework travels through technical plans and indicators that leave little room for women's own accounts of insecurity. The second is a belonging gap: women's peace work in the North often happens through faith, family and community networks that national plans do not recognise as security actors. The third is a resource gap: action plans are rarely funded or localised. The article argues that WPS will matter in northern Nigeria only when it is rebuilt from the ground up, with women's local knowledge and networks at its centre.

detail.abstract: When governments are unable to cover their fiscal deficits via taxation they often resort to printing more money for their financing needs. This excess supply of money leads to inflation which acts like a tax on whoever holds currency. This study designs a tractable model focusing on the optimal level of inflation such that how much should the government print before inflation burden becomes disproportionate? The distributional term is not imposed on the system, but emerges from the budget constraint depending on the covariance of welfare across household groups and how much each group's share of the currency stock differs from its share of the taxable base. For Pakistan in 2024, the poorest 40% of the households possess 25.1% of the currency while contributing only 9.0% of the taxable base in 2024, an increasing disparity compared to 2021. Optimal inflation lies between 1.0 and 7.4 per cent when incidence of tax is ignored. It falls to about one-third of that at moderate inequality aversion, and to zero under stronger distributional weights. Semi-elasticity of money demand could not be specified and therefore results are reported over a range.

detail.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's 2024 National Primary Drinking Water Regulation for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) set enforceable limits of 4.0 parts per trillion for PFOA and PFOS. EPA has since proposed (May 2026) to keep these two limits while allowing eligible systems to extend compliance to 2031. Billions of dollars in federal grants and loans are available to help, yet small water systems (those serving 10,000 people or fewer) are the least able to use them, because applying requires system-specific technical documentation they rarely have the staff to produce. This working paper proposes a four-step diagnostic framework that builds that documentation using only public, nationally consistent data: (1) a contamination profile from EPA's Fifth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule (UCMR 5); (2) selection of an EPA-designated Best Available Technology (BAT); (3) a population-scaled cost estimate from EPA's Work Breakdown Structure cost models; and (4) a match against applicable federal and state funding programs. An application to small systems in the Raritan River watershed, New Jersey, illustrates the approach. Because every input is public and available nationwide, the framework can be applied to any small system in the United States at screening level, turning a general federal mandate into a specific, fundable action plan.

detail.abstract: Over the past six decades, Cuban migration has evolved through shifting geopolitical constraints, economic restructuring, and changing opportunity structures, producing a diaspora that is both historically layered and rapidly transforming. Drawing on original survey and interview data from Cuban migrants in Miami and Madrid, this study examines remittance dynamics through the lens of demographic characteristics, economic position, gender differences, and household structures. Findings reveal both continuities and divergences: Cuban migrants in Miami remit higher average amounts and demonstrate greater resilience in remittance capacity, while women in both cities send a higher proportion of their income compared to men. Across both contexts, remittances remain vital lifelines, sustaining families’ basic needs and extending over long periods of time. The article further explores how the COVID-19 pandemic (declared a pandemic in 2020) and the temporary suspension of Western Union (November 2021 – January 2023) accelerated a transition in remittance channels, reinforcing informal mechanisms while spurring the expansion of digital transfers, combo shipments, and mobile top-ups. These practices underscore remittances as both economic lifelines and expressions of transnational care. Yet, the uneven rise of digital remittances exposes persistent inequalities as access remains stratified by income, age, education, and digital literacy.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we derive the asymptotic normality of the recently proposed cluster jackknife instrumental variables estimator (CJIVE) in clustered instrumental variable models with many instruments. We allow the dimension of the exogenous controls to diverge and establish a sufficient rate condition under which the bias induced by their inclusion is asymptotically negligible. We further construct a ratio-consistent estimator of the asymptotic variance, thereby enabling feasible inference for CJIVE. Numerical simulations and an empirical application illustrate the finite-sample performance and practical relevance of the proposed procedure.

detail.abstract: Software-defined networking (SDN) separates the control plane from the data plane and places network intelligence in logically centralized controllers, which creates a natural point at which resource allocation and traffic management decisions can be made on the basis of global network state. As traffic volumes, application diversity, and service-level requirements continue to grow, hand-crafted heuristics and static optimization models become increasingly difficult to maintain. This paper reviews peer-reviewed work on intelligent resource allocation and traffic management in SDN, covering architectural foundations, centralized traffic engineering in production wide-area networks, machine learning and deep reinforcement learning approaches to routing and resource management, graph-based network modeling, and network slicing. The review identifies recurring limitations: heavy reliance on simulated evaluation, weak generalization across topologies and traffic regimes, limited safety guarantees during online learning, controller scalability, and a lack of standardized benchmarks and interpretability. Building on this analysis, the paper proposes a conceptual layered framework in which telemetry, learned network models, constrained decision policies, and verified enforcement are coupled in a closed control loop with explicit safety and explainability mechanisms. The framework is offered as a structure for future research and has not been empirically validated; no experiments, datasets, or results are reported. The paper concludes with practical implications for network operators and a prioritized research agenda covering offline and safe reinforcement learning, federated learning, graph-based models, and reproducible evaluation.

detail.abstract: The United States globally leads in developing new, innovative drugs. American taxpayers and private payors also pay far more for patented drugs than foreign counterparts do. The Trump Administration is seeking to require pharmaceutical firms to lower US drug prices while it threatens sanctions against foreign countries unless they pay more for US-produced drugs. Drug price controls, however, would undermine innovation, thereby harming both drug producers and consumers. Fortunately, political economy considerations incentivize foreign governments to lift patented drug prices when agreements support their domestic industrial policies and life sciences ambitions. Replacing coercive price-fixing and regulatory friction with reciprocal trade and regulatory synergy would foster a robust, equitable innovation ecosystem that sustainably finances future medical cures. The 2025 US-UK agreement on pharmaceutical pricing demonstrates the achievability of such agreements. This paper outlines frameworks for future agreements aimed at increasing foreign contributions to pharmaceutical innovation and applies them to the European Union (EU).

detail.abstract: Training Needs Analysis (TNA) is an initial stage in the human resource development (HRD) training and development cycle that identifies competency gaps and determines whether training is truly the solution to a performance problem. This article reviews the literature on the definition and objectives of TNA, its position in the training and development cycle, the three levels of needs analysis (organizational, individual, and task), and the role of organizational analysis in linking strategy, key performance indicators (KPIs), and training needs. The review then covers internal and external factors, data collection methods, the roles of stakeholders, the determination of whether a problem requires training through gap and root cause analysis, trainee and organizational readiness for training transfer, the use of HR analytics and artificial intelligence (AI), and common errors in TNA. The review indicates that effective TNA starts from the organization's strategic challenges, uses data triangulation across multiple sources and stakeholders, traces root causes before deciding on training or nontraining interventions, and takes trainee readiness and work-environment support into account. HR analytics and AI can complement, rather than replace, existing TNA methods, provided that data quality, ethics, and human oversight are maintained.

detail.abstract: Long-short strategies can exhibit exceptional monthly Sharpe ratios, yet their performance deteriorates sharply at longer horizons. Across anomaly and machine-learning portfolios, we document a strong positive relation between monthly Sharpe ratios and long-horizon variance ratios: strategies that perform best at short horizons accumulate risk fastest over time. This pattern arises primarily because the correlation between long and short legs declines with the horizon, undermining the risk reduction from their high monthly correlation. A factor decomposition links this deterioration to high-variance-ratio factors with opposite-signed exposures that also account for much of long-short expected returns. Monthly performance can therefore substantially overstate longer-horizon risk-adjusted performance.

detail.abstract:
Purpose
This paper addresses the underexplored issue of museum staff wellbeing, a significant gap despite museums increasing role in fostering visitor wellbeing. It investigates how structured interventions mitigate stress and anxiety among museum personnel, enhancing their workplace experience and contributing to improved organisational culture and performance within cultural institutions. 
Design/methodology/approach 
An eight-week action-research study, the ASBA programme based on a research protocol approved by the Ethics Committee of the University Milano-Bicocca, and involved staff from three museums. A mixed-methods approach collected quantitative data and qualitative insights. Interventions included Mindfulness, Art Therapy, Chair Yoga, and Nature+Art. 
Findings 
Quantitative data revealed a significant reduction in staff trait anxiety, with Chair Yoga particularly decreasing state anxiety. Qualitative findings corroborated these improvements, showing a progressive transformation in workplace culture. Participants transitioned from initial scepticism to enhanced engagement, emotional awareness, conflict resolution, and cohesive team dynamics, fostering collective purpose and professional mastery. 
Originality 
This study represents a pioneering effort to systematically develop and evaluate tailored wellbeing interventions for museum staff within an ecologically valid museum setting. By focusing on the often-overlooked mental health of museum professionals, the ASBA Project advocates for a holistic institutional commitment that benefits both employees and the broader museum ecosystem.

detail.abstract: The mandatory nature of the death sentence for murder in Kenya has been the subject of significant constitutional controversy, particularly following the Supreme Court's decision in Francis Karioko Muruatetu & another v Republic. This paper examines whether the mandatory death sentence prescribed under section 204 of the Penal Code is constitutionally invalid, with particular focus on the relationship between Parliament's legislative authority and the judiciary's constitutional and interpretive functions. The paper adopts a doctrinal legal research method, analyzing the Constitution of Kenya, relevant statutory provisions and Kenyan judicial decisions concerning the death penalty, judicial discretion, sentencing, constitutional supremacy and the hierarchy of laws. The paper argues that article 26(3) of the Constitution expressly recognizes that intentional deprivation of life may be authorized by the Constitution or other written law, thereby providing constitutional space for Parliament to prescribe the death penalty. It further argues that the mandatory use of the word “shall” in section 204 of the Penal Code does not, by itself, violate judicial discretion, since judicial discretion is exercised within the limits established by law. The paper also examines the claims that mandatory sentencing violates individualized sentencing, the right to appeal, equality before the law, human dignity and access to justice. It argues that these principles should be considered in relation to both the convicted person and the victim whose right to life was unlawfully taken. The paper concludes that, where section 204 is viewed within the constitutional allocation of legislative and judicial authority, the mandatory death sentence can be understood as a constitutionally valid legislative penalty. It therefore calls for continued constitutional and judicial examination of the distinction between the validity of the death penalty itself and the constitutionality of its mandatory application.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how Hyundai Motor Company’s electric vehicle strategy has influenced its competitive position in the United States. It focuses on the company’s expansion of U.S.-based production, investment in electric vehicle manufacturing capacity, pricing and product strategy, and efforts to respond to changes in the U.S. policy and competitive environment. Using secondary data from company, industry and government sources, the study applies Porter’s Generic Strategies, economies of scale, return on investment analysis, and competitor benchmarking to evaluate Hyundai’s strategic position. The analysis suggests that localisation and expanded production capacity can strengthen Hyundai’s competitiveness by reducing production and logistics costs, improving access to policy incentives, and supporting greater scale in the U.S. market. Benchmarking against major competitors further highlights the importance of pricing, product differentiation and manufacturing scale in determining competitive performance. However, the strategy also involves substantial capital commitments and remains exposed to changing consumer demand, competitive pressure and policy conditions. The paper concludes that Hyundai’s U.S. EV strategy has the potential to strengthen its long-term competitive position, although the financial returns from these investments depend on successful capacity utilisation and sustained growth in electric vehicle demand.

detail.abstract: This note studies how the sequencing of national regulations can affect platform choice in global digital markets. I consider a content creator choosing between a global and a local platform. The global platform initially embeds a foreign regulatory requirement into its architecture, creating a compliance cost for creators using it. When a domestic regulation is subsequently introduced, however, the global platform can partly reuse its pre-existing compliance infrastructure. This regulatory head start may increase its relative attractiveness and can even induce a switch in creators' preferred single-homing platform. I also allow creators to multi-home and show how declining translation and localisation costs, including those associated with AI-assisted translation, expand the scope for cross-platform distribution. The framework is motivated by COPPA and the 2026 proposal for an EU KIDS Act.

detail.abstract: Starting in 1989, the Banque de France maintains a corporate information system known as FIBEN. This unique system combines information on financial statements (consolidated and unconsolidated), bank credit exposures, bank-firm relationships, legal events, payment defaults, ownership structures, equity links, CEOs, and credit ratings. Although FIBEN has become a key data source for empirical microeconomic research on French non-financial firms, no comprehensive guideline exists for users and potential users. This paper provides a guide to the database, documenting its extensive coverage, strong representativeness, collection process, methodological changes, and structural breaks over time, thereby highlighting its value for both policy-oriented and academic research. We also benchmark FIBEN against alternative administrative datasets.

detail.abstract: We introduce a rigorous geometric model of market capacity for crowded alpha strategies. A market with d independent risk factors is represented as a d-dimensional Euclidean factor space. A strategy is a unit vector describing its normalized risk exposure. Under linear isotropic temporary price impact and a worst-case sign-alignment convention, the adverse pairwise crowding effect between two strategies is proportional to the absolute inner product of their exposure vectors. A pairwise crowding constraint therefore becomes exactly a projective spherical-code constraint. We show that the maximum number of strategies that can coexist under a pairwise correlation cap is precisely the maximum size of a projective spherical code. Using classical packing bounds, we obtain exponential asymptotic bounds for pairwise market capacity. We then prove a complementary aggregate-capacity theorem: under an aggregate Sharpe-ratio constraint, a Welch-type argument implies that capacity is at most linear in the number of independent risk factors. Thus, pairwise correlation limits alone can dramatically overstate true market capacity. The paper provides a clean bridge between high-dimensional spherical geometry, Welch bounds, equiangular tight frames, and quantitative portfolio crowding.

detail.abstract: Monetary policy works largely through expectations: core transmission channels, including long-term yields, mortgage rates, and investment, depend on expected future policy. Markets interpret current choices as informative about the central bank's realtime readings of the economy–readings that persist and guide future policy. When choosing a rate, the central bank takes as given how markets interpret its decisions. However, its systematic behavior shapes that interpretation, and hence how strongly mistakes in those readings affect the economy. We show that this creates a timeinconsistency problem: optimal meeting-by-meeting policy can leave market expectations excessively sensitive to policy surprises, amplifying the effects of those mistakes. We quantify this mechanism's importance in an extended New Keynesian model estimated using macroeconomic data, Federal Reserve forecasts, natural-output uncertainty estimates, and inflation-swap responses to policy surprises. The optimal ex ante rule substantially reduces output-gap volatility by responding less aggressively overall, especially to estimates of natural output.

title: Relative Minimal Module Basis for Structural–Regime Theory: Closure of Systemic Results, Constructive Irreducibility, and the Dynamical–Fisher–Statistical Interface
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Relative Minimal Module Basis for Structural–Regime Theory: Closure of Systemic Results, Constructive Irreducibility, and the Dynamical–Fisher–Statistical Interface

detail.abstract:
This paper studies a relative metatheoretical problem for structural–regime theory: under a common mathematical background and a fixed partition of semantic roles, does a theory spanning geometry, information, dynamics, and statistical observation possess an irreducible common modular basis? Here, “minimality” is not interpreted as the number of axioms, which can be altered arbitrarily by logical conjunction. Instead, we define a common background theory, semantic closure, role-preserving module representations, and a relative module-basis rank. Minimality is thereby recast as an irreducibility problem within a fixed class of semantic interfaces.

We introduce four interface modules: the geometric interface B_G (Markov–Fisher naturality); the information–factor interface B_I (Markov information cascades, scale separation, nondegenerate mechanism roles, and factor-level distinguishability); the dynamical–boundary interface B_D (local structural stratification, nondegenerate critical sets, transverse crossing, and local normal forms); and the statistical-observation interface B_O (Fréchet differentiability of the statistical trace and nondegeneracy along the switching direction). The common background imposes only technical conditions concerning measurability, regularity, finite information quantities, and measure selection; when invariant measures are nonunique, the selected measure is explicitly specified by a measure selector.

We obtain six groups of principal results. First, under the Markov cascade W → X → F → U, we establish the exact information-deficit decomposition H(W) − I(W;U) = H(W|X) + I(W;X|F) + I(W;F|U). Second, on a regular critical set, we prove that transverse crossing produces a sign change of a defining function, yielding local identification of a regime boundary. Third, if the parameter difference between two sides has a nonzero leading term aτ^q and the composite statistical trace T has a nonzero Fréchet derivative in the a direction, then the statistical visibility order is exactly preserved as q. Fourth, defining the Fisher intrinsic energy in the switching direction by E_sw = g_F(θ*)(a,a), we prove its coordinate invariance and monotone contraction under Markov coarse-graining. Fifth, we establish a joint-generation theorem for the four interfaces and construct directional witnesses for each interface, thereby proving strong irreducibility. Sixth, under a fixed role system, we define a relative module-basis rank and prove Rank_mod = 4.

Furthermore, we package the prior results on Fisher–B6, information–factor structure, structural switching, periodic observability, and faithful statistical representation into an explicit core conclusion package of the theory, and prove relative semantic closure of this package under the four-interface basis. For results at the exactness level, we explicitly add calibration conditions rather than claiming an unconditional extension. The paper thus distinguishes two levels: “axiom reduction,” which studies conditional necessity for individual conclusions, and “joint metatheory,” which studies the irreducible semantic basis shared by multiple conclusions. This is a purely theoretical study and involves no empirical data, numerical simulation, or parameter fitting.

title: A Unified Metatheory of Structural Claim Transformation: Recoverability, Obstructions, and Reachability — Series Synthesis, Transformation Certificates, Semantic Invariants, Certification Gaps, Obstruction Spectra, Module–Obstruction Dual Bases, and Computability Boundaries
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: A Unified Metatheory of Structural Claim Transformation: Recoverability, Obstructions, and Reachability — Series Synthesis, Transformation Certificates, Semantic Invariants, Certification Gaps, Obstruction Spectra, Module–Obstruction Dual Bases, and Computability Boundaries

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.

detail.abstract:
This paper is a purely theoretical study combining a series-level synthesis with an independent metatheory. Taking seven theoretical works, 2026ay–2026be, as input, it reconstructs their logical lineage and then upgrades the question "can a structural claim change its theoretical role?" into a transformation problem with explicit semantic objects, role equivalence, generation–recovery relations, and failure boundaries. Within the declared class of structural claims, it uses conditional reasoning (CR), structural grounding (SG), and framework unification (FU) as the principal mechanism language.

First, a basic recoverability criterion on the role quotient is given, followed by a structural-invariant obstruction-screening theorem and a conditional completeness result. A situation in which nonequivalent source objects are folded into equivalent target representations becomes a falsifiable failure mode of recovery. Second, a typed calculus of transformation certificates is established, recording additional conditions, enlarged structure, mechanism word, generation–recovery correspondence, semantic validity domain, failure boundary, and non-circular dependence. Under explicit congruence and gluing-coherence conditions, certificates can be composed, and a union–inverse-image propagation law for failure boundaries is obtained. Third, the paper strictly separates "the transformation does not exist mathematically" from "the current certificate language cannot cover the transformation." For the semantic feasible domain Feas, the certificate-effective domain Eff, and the certification gap Gap, it proves X_A = Obst_Sem ⊔ Gap_L ⊔ Eff_L, thereby distinguishing genuine semantic obstructions from removable expressive gaps.

Fourth, an obstruction-spectrum theory is developed. For objects coverable by a complete certificate language, a minimal deletion-obstruction family and an obstruction order are defined. Under module monotonicity, the minimal obstruction-deletion family and the minimal support family satisfy classical blocker duality. A one-hot identity matrix is only a special coordinate realization of an obstruction of order 1; higher-order synergetic irreducibility is characterized by obstruction order greater than 1. Fifth, an expressive-capacity theory for transformation certificate languages is introduced, using the known strict separation between tree-like and general Resolution as external calibration. Sixth, the computability boundary is characterized: unbounded reachability is recursively enumerable, fixed-length truncations are decidable, and under an effective embedding of first-order theoremhood, transformation reachability is r.e.-complete. A Rice-type argument shows that no uniformly total computable scheme can simultaneously generate and verify certificates soundly and completely.

Finally, the metatheory is instantiated on 2026ay–2026be, with a finite target registry and a checkable priority-evidence structure. Priority is restricted to the organization of transformation, recoverability, obstructions, support, and computability boundaries into one provable object system under explicitly specified structural claims, role-preserving semantics, certificate languages, and a common background. All completeness, minimality, irreducibility, and priority statements are restricted to explicitly declared model classes.

detail.abstract:
Traditional macroeconomic long-wave theories often struggle with imprecise cycle durations and lack a physical basis for their period. This paper presents a cross-scale Fractal Orbital-Generational Model that unifies a measured biological clock, systemic scale effects, and institutional dynamics. The period is taken from the human generation interval-the mean age of parents at childbirth, measured at roughly 25-31 years across societies and over the past 250,000 years-rather than fitted to historical data; it is the social-scale consequence of a reproductive physiology shaped by the solar and lunar light cycles under which humans evolved. This 28-30 year clock governs generational turnover, institutional memory dissipation, and capital accumulation. We formalize the framework as a noise-driven damped oscillator whose natural period is the generation interval, and introduce two foundational qualifiers to this natural baseline:
(i) Institutional Counter-Forces: human organizational structures, technology, and
counter-cyclical policies act as macro-dampeners, dynamically resisting and altering the
expression of natural cycle clearing.
(ii) Systemic Inertia (Scale Effect): grounded in the law of large numbers, small nations are
dominated by exogenous shocks, whereas hyper-scale societies (large population/economic
inertia) are predicted to show the intrinsic 30-year rhythm more clearly.
In addition to century-scale historical alignment (1899 → 1929 → 1958 → 1989 → 2019), we
give an operational definition of a realignment point—an irreversible transition of the prevailing
geopolitical-economic order, as distinct from the depth of a downturn—which separates
within-regime shocks (e.g., 2008) from regime transitions. Under this definition, a forecast for
China, expressed in public forum replies in 2016–2017 and preserved with third-party timestamps
by an independent web archive, identified the second half of 2019 as the turning point (Appendix
A). The record that followed fits a three-stage pattern: endogenous fragility surfaced in 2019, an
exogenous shock (COVID-19) acted as the trigger in 2020, and an irreversible order transition
followed—on a global scale that the original forecast did not anticipate. A pre-specified
cross-country spectral test, however, does not confirm the model's quantitative predictions: output
growth in 30 countries shows no excess power at 25–35 years, and neither output nor credit
shows the predicted increase with country size; credit-to-GDP in 11 economies shows only a
weak, exploratory tendency toward a peak near 28 years. Classified with a fixed dating rule, the
histories of three hyper-scale societies give node onsets near 1898–1929–1958–1989–2019 for
China, near 1900–1929–1957–1990–2016/19 for India and, from the 1830s, intervals of 29–36
years for the United States, with documented exceptions; a supplementary spectral analysis gives
India a peak at 29 years, not individually significant, while Japan, a mid-sized comparison case, is
less regular. Finally, the model yields a testable forward prediction identifying ~2049 as the next
global structural realignment point.

detail.abstract:
Why do some societies emerge from systemic crisis faster than others? This paper argues that crisis pressure alone is not the decisive factor; the interaction between pressure and the openness of social selection, together with the persistence of that openness after the crisis, should be. I define five separately measurable components (selection pressure, openness, generational adaptive capacity, institutional retention, and destruction), derive seven falsifiable predictions, specify an estimable model with a pressure-by-openness interaction, and set out placebo, timing, and case-selection rules for testing it. The paper does not estimate the model. It reports pilot descriptive evidence from verified sources: 2025 SIPRI military-burden data, OECD mobility indicators, and historical and contemporary cases (Finland, South Korea, Poland, Israel, the United States after 1945, and Ukraine). Three pilot observations follow. 

Military burden in Ukraine is about five times that of the next highest country in the comparison set, which makes a continuous pressure measure fragile. Headline absolute upward mobility, as in Korea, coexists with substantial relative persistence, so it is an unreliable proxy for openness. Wartime selection became durable where institutional rules changed, as with the GI Bill and RAND, which is the retention condition on which the Ukrainian test depends. For Ukraine, I identify observable indicators that distinguish functional opening from patronage in civil-service appointments.

detail.abstract: We discuss the role of fiduciary duty in financial economics. We first demonstrate that there are di.erent levels of depth of engagement with the content of the definition of fiduciary duty in the financial literature. Most contributors tacitly presume a narrow definition of fiduciary duty or merely mention it in passing. Only some authors provide more detailed definitions. And very few authors explicitly discuss the values at play in di.erent definitions of fiduciary duty. The concept of fiduciary duty, while a key normative assumption underlying investment practice, seems to hide in plain sight in the current debates. We argue that deeper engagement with the concept of fiduciary duty is desirable. Such deeper engagement improves conceptual clarity, comparability across analyses, and transparency about normative assumptions. Doing so also contributes to responsible financial economics understood as the obligation to make normatively consequential assumptions explicit.

detail.abstract: Debates on artificial intelligence and international politics are dominated by the rivalry between the United States and China, which leaves out how other countries become dependent on infrastructures, models and rules they do not control. This article asks how AI reconfigures structural power in the global political economy and why it fragments its governance. It reports a systematic review following PRISMA 2020: 1,763 records from Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection (2018-2026) were deduplicated to 1,199 and screened by two independent automated screeners (rule-based and zero-shot natural language inference; κ = 0.457), with adjudication of conflicts. Of these, 330 studies were mapped through keyword co-occurrence, and a core of 49 informed a qualitative synthesis. The literature forms five clusters, led by sovereignty and the Global South and by great-power regulatory competition, while work on data extraction remains dispersed. Building on Strange, Gilpin and Zuboff, the article proposes the Geopolitical AI Power Framework (GAPF), in which structural power asymmetry, techno-nationalist fragmentation and surveillance capitalism externalities reinforce one another and produce structural lock-in. Lock-in is a tendency, not a destiny: semi-peripheral countries can still shape their position through capabilities, negotiation and regional coordination.

detail.abstract: The aim of this paper is to explore the public policy options available for restructuring key aspects of the UK banking and financial system so as to better facilitate the local growth effects of devolved governance. In order to do this, we examine three cases of different models of state development banks (SDBs), KfW in Germany, Bpifrance in France and EIB at the European Level, which provide powerful insights as to how the UK institutional system can be adapted to best ensure that governance devolution is also associated with enhanced local and regional growth. Key insights relate to the scale of capital, the need for direct and ongoing access to clients and customers, investment risk-pricing as well as capacity building and capability enhancement.

detail.abstract: How do U.S. monetary policy shocks affect long-term interest rates in emerging market economies, and why do these effects differ across exchange rate regimes? We address this question using empirical evidence and a two-country DSGE model. Local projection estimates for a panel of 25 advanced and emerging economies over 2006-2022 show that contractionary U.S. monetary shocks significantly increase sovereign term premia under pegged and managed exchange rate regimes, while the effects are negligible under floating regimes. To explain these findings, we develop a DSGE model with segmented bond markets and financially constrained intermediaries. The model shows that exchange rate pegs shift the adjustment to domestic interest rates, eroding intermediary net worth, tightening leverage constraints, and amplifying increases in term premia and contractions in investment and output. We further derive a modified uncovered interest parity condition linking UIP deviations to the expected path of term premia, providing a theoretical explanation for the exchange-rate-regime dependence of international monetary spillovers.

detail.abstract: Economic headroom is the distance by which a boundary-relevant position exceeds a consequential requirement. Errors in both components mean that positive reported headroom need not imply a positive target. This paper organizes measurement-error, partial-identification and simultaneous-inference tools into lower safety certificates. Its empirical form combines one-sided split-conformal bounds by Bonferroni under exchangeability of calibration and target overstatements. The guarantee is marginal joint coverage for one target’s predeclared constraint family, not posterior safety, conditional safety among issued certificates, or simultaneous coverage across future dates. JYDB performance express reports matched to later annual statements yield 99.12 percent joint equity-and-profit coverage in 1,938 chronological pseudo-test firm-years during 2022–2024, with 78.90 percent certified and five point-estimate false-safe cases reduced to one. FY2025 internal post-freeze confirmation yields 98.54 percent coverage and no false-safe joint certificates. Reweighting and later annual comparatives provide further descriptive checks. Rolling three-year calibrations cover 94.6–99.6 percent over seven test years, including a year below 95 percent. Repeated firms, common-year shocks and changing reporter composition prevent these observations from validating exchangeability or proving nominal deployment coverage. The empirical target is the later audited-report benchmark, not unobserved economic truth. The contribution is an integrated measurement-and-decision protocol with explicit scope conditions, not a new covariance inequality or causal design.

detail.abstract: Dynamic models in finance and economics commonly assume that ambiguity preferences are stationary across payoff horizons, yet there is little direct evidence for this restriction. We test the stationarity of ambiguity preferences in a counterbalanced experiment in which participants evaluate the same decision problems with either immediate payoff realization or realization delayed by eight weeks. Ambiguity attitudes are elicited using binary choices and probability equivalents across low-and moderatelikelihood gains, losses, and mixed prospects, with all decisions implemented under real monetary incentives. We find strong evidence consistent with stationarity. Ambiguity attitudes differ little across horizons, and equivalence tests rule out economically meaningful timing effects. This stability does not reflect weak ambiguity preferences. Instead, we recover a pronounced four-fold pattern of ambiguity aversion and seeking across likelihood levels and outcome domains. Individual ambiguity classifications are also no less consistent across the eight-week interval than across elicitation methods within a session. Our findings support the use of stationary ambiguity preferences in dynamic models and show that substantial heterogeneity in ambiguity attitudes can coexist with temporal stationarity.

detail.abstract: The rise in unit profits has been a major contributor to price inflation across the euro area in the post-pandemic period. A widely cited explanation in the literature attributes this trend to post-pandemic supply bottlenecks, which temporarily allowed firms in key sectors to exercise market power, thereby increasing profit margins. An additional argument posits that the degree of competition in these sectors plays a structural role in shaping and driving unit profit growth. The present study empirically tests that hypothesis, using Greece as a case study—an economy within the euro area that saw particularly sharp increases in prices and unit profits during the post-pandemic years. To this end, annual panel data from Greece's economic sectors covering the period 2017–2023 are used. The econometric analysis confirms this hypothesis, indicating that the market power, proxied by sectoral concentration rates, has been a significant determinant of profit and inflation dynamics in the period under consideration.

detail.abstract: This paper studies system vulnerability conditional on an observed cross-sectional distribution of economic headroom, the distance between each institution's position and a consequential boundary. The object is not whether latent boundaries can be recovered from behavior but how a measured distribution maps into first passage, cascades, and the value of reallocating capacity. Average headroom is generally insufficient. When institutions' idiosyncratic shocks are independent with log-concave densities, a mean-preserving spread of headroom raises the probability of a first boundary hit; without independence the result can fail. For the network channel the relevant object is the transmission mass at or below each headroom level: expected one-step cascade loss equals the expected transmission mass that a shock overwhelms, so states are ordered by this function over the range shocks can reach. A centrality-weighted lower-tail average is sufficient only together with the transmission mass in the tail, and its sufficiency depends on the shock law and maintained model. Crossing transmission-mass functions rule out a universal shock-law-independent vulnerability ordering, not every scalar summary for a fixed model. A planner equalizes marginal systemic benefits, whose network part is an institution's transmission weight times the shock density at its headroom, so equal buffers are not optimal in general and two allocations with identical inequality can differ in vulnerability. A calibration evaluates the vulnerability functional under common random numbers: the same spread placed on network hubs rather than on peripheral institutions raises vulnerability by 19 percent, while a large transfer toward the hubs also raises it because it thins every other buffer. An empirical protocol for observed capacity proxies is given; the paper reports no estimates.

detail.abstract: Securing affordable and sustainable housing is a key challenge for an ecological economics that sets itself the goal of social-ecological provisioning for a good life for all within planetary boundaries. Addressing this challenge requires a more efficient use of existing housing space in cities. Feminist (ecological) economists have long demonstrated that the gendered division of labour is evident within the ’private sphere’ of the household. We propose that shared housing, i.e. people living together within a household who are not all related or in romantic relationships, is an interesting case where the social-ecological provisioning of care and housing intersect. We investigate the spatial dimensions of care, provisioning, and everyday life by means of a mixed methods case study on shared housing in Vienna, combining statistical analysis, focus groups, and expert interviews. More concretely, we analyse the status quo, potentials, and challenges of shared housing to contribute to social-ecological transformation, including the recognition, reduction, and redistribution of unpaid care work, as well as policies to unlock these potentials.

detail.abstract: For two decades, legal scholarship has described the United States Information and Educational Exchange Act of 1948, the Smith-Mundt Act, as the source of a ban on the domestic dissemination of the government’s international information materials. The 1948 text contains no such ban. Its one sentence about access at home required that the program’s press releases and radio scripts be available for examination by the American press and radio and to Members of Congress. Congress wanted oversight of the program, the wording on access was meant to spare the State Department a “deluge of requests” for translations of everything it released, and the bill’s Senate sponsor said the aim was to make the information available “to everybody.” The prohibition was written in 1972 and enhanced in 1985. This response sets out the record of 1945 to 1948, shows that the reading given the Act then held until shortly before the prohibition of 1972, and examines how the literature, having conceded that the 1948 text contains no prohibition, inferred one anyway. It takes no position on whether a domestic restriction is good policy. Its argument is that the history offered for one is wrong and material to subsequent claims.

detail.abstract: We offer new empirical facts and insights into the determinants and dynamics of food and housing insecurity in an advanced market economy, based on a novel administrative panel data set from France's largest food assistance charity that is unique in its comprehensive coverage of low-income households-in particular of homeless individuals. We document several findings. First, children and teenagers are vastly over-represented in both food and housing insecurity. Second, these situations are largely transient, though a very large fraction of households is exposed to the risk of experiencing them at some point in the near future. Third, flows into and out of food and housing insecurity are asymmetric: Inflows are highly sensitive to local macroeconomic conditions and policies, whereas outflows only depend on individual characteristics, with an especially strong duration dependence. Fourth, the high inflation rates of the past few years are responsible for about half of the fast rising rates of homelessness in France since 2018.

detail.abstract: How quickly should a firm reconfigure sourcing after a policy shock? The usual answer is to diversify at once. That advice is incomplete when shocks arrive in sequence and the next shock does not spare the origins chosen after the first. We examine this problem among U.S. solar installers that faced two federal tariffs. The 2014 duties taxed Chinese-origin modules and rewarded geographic diversification. The 2018 safeguard taxed virtually every origin and reduced the value of that geographic hedge. Using project-level installation records from 2010 to 2024, we measure how many quarters each installer waited, in each local market, before reducing source-country concentration after 2014. Installers that waited longer gained relative local share after 2018. A one-standard-deviation longer wait is associated with a 1.11 percentage-point higher post-2018 share, or 21.5 percent of the pre-shock mean. Mechanism tests show that they used historically important suppliers more intensively, improved product and technology mix, and completed more projects, without charging reliably higher prices. The return to waiting is larger where the installer already had a longer collaboration history with its manufacturers and already operated in more local markets. These findings suggest that resilience under repeated shocks depends not only on how quickly firms reconfigure supply chains, but also on which relationship-specific capabilities are preserved during adjustment.

detail.abstract: Background: The EpiSense National Grid proposal [1] would add a forecast-based alert type to threshold alerting in U.S. syndromic surveillance, on the premise that alerts built on forecasts can fire earlier than alerts on raw counts. That premise has not been tested against known outbreak onsets. Objective: To measure whether forecast-based alerts detect outbreaks earlier than threshold alerts at equal false-alarm rates, and whether any gain comes from looking ahead. Methods: A stochastic 50-node SEIRS simulation with known true incidence generated 24 independent worlds in each of six scenarios (reporting noise, delay and seasonal synchrony varied). Thresholds for each alert type were calibrated on validation seasons to fixed false-alarm rates and evaluated on test seasons. Compared were a z-score threshold, CUSUM, smoothed-count alerts, forecast-based alerts from a GCN-LSTM and a ridge auto regression, a union of threshold and forecast alerts, and oracle controls with raw-count foresight and noise-free expected counts. Results: At 0.5 false alarms per node-season in the baseline scenario, GCN-LSTM alerts led the threshold z-score by 0.81 [0.72, 0.91] weeks (paired, mean and 95% CI). However, CUSUM on raw counts led by 0.81 [0.70, 0.92] weeks, and the GCN-LSTM was no earlier than CUSUM (difference 0.00 [-0.09, 0.10]). The lead did not grow with forecast horizon, and a noise-free current expected count with no look ahead led by 1.02 [0.95, 1.10] weeks, more than any forecast. The union alert added nothing to the GCN-LSTM alone at matched false-alarm rate, and its false-alarm burden was about 0.61 of the sum of its parts. A ridge forecast captured only a fraction of the gain. Conclusions: In this simulation the earlier detection of forecast-based alerts came from noise filtering, not foresight, and could be matched by better-designed threshold statistics. All findings are synthetic proof-of-concept results.

detail.abstract: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) represents a major institutional step toward the economic integration of the African continent. Yet the creation of a continental market for goods and services cannot be fully achieved without a corresponding integration of the people, skills and professional capacities that sustain economic activity. Although the African Union (AU) has developed important legal and policy instruments concerning the free movement of persons, labour migration, the right of residence and establishment, skills recognition and social protection, African professional mobility remains fragmented by national regulations, regional arrangements, administrative barriers and insufficient mechanisms for the recognition and portability of qualifications and social rights. This article argues that Africa's integration agenda should move beyond the traditional distinction between trade integration and migration governance and develop a broader concept of continental professional integration. This concept refers to the progressive construction of an African professional space in which workers, professionals, entrepreneurs, researchers and service providers can move, work, provide services, have their qualifications recognised, access information and benefit from adequate legal protection across African borders. The article proposes the African Organization for Mobility and Migration (OAMM) as a civil-society institutional mechanism capable of contributing to this objective. OAMM is conceived neither as an organ of the African Union nor as an institution of the AfCFTA, but as an independent pan-African research, knowledge, coordination and digital innovation platform. Its proposed functions include an African Observatory of Professional Mobility, a continental skills and qualifications platform, a digital professional skills passport, a legal and regulatory information system, a worker-protection mechanism and an African research network on labour mobility. The article develops a legal and institutional framework linking the AfCFTA, the AU Free Movement Protocol, the Migration Policy Framework for Africa, regional economic communities and international labour standards. It argues that the effectiveness of continental economic integration depends increasingly on the capacity of African legal systems to facilitate the circulation and recognition of human capital. The central proposition is that the next stage of African integration should not merely be the movement of African goods across African borders, but the effective circulation, recognition and protection of African skills and professional capacities.

detail.abstract: North American cruise routes cross jurisdictions frequently. On a single voyage, a vessel may move between Canadian and United States waters several times, for example between Vancouver and Alaska, along the New England-Atlantic Canada coast, or through the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence system. Each crossing changes the rules on pilotage, incident reporting and regulatory oversight, while cruise crews are highly multinational and multilingual. This paper argues that points of jurisdictional change are an under-examined source of operational safety risk. The risk is greatest where differing legal allocations of navigational responsibility meet language barriers on the bridge and among safety-critical personnel. Drawing on the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, the International Safety Management Code, the International Convention on Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping for Seafarers, Canadian and United States domestic law, and Canadian marine investigation findings, the paper makes three contributions. First, it identifies four categories of transition risk: authority, reporting, linguistic and procedural. Second, it proposes an integrated communication and compliance model for managing these risks within a vessel's existing safety management system, and illustrates it on a Great Lakes-St. Lawrence itinerary. Third, it offers practical recommendations for operators and regulators. The paper concludes that coordination between authorities alone cannot close the safety gap. A standardized onboard communication protocol is needed to make "one voyage, two regimes" operationally safe.

detail.abstract:
We study stochastic dynamic matching with abandonment, a fundamental model in which agents of different types arrive over time, may abandon the market while waiting, and can be matched in pairs for rewards that depend on their types. No online policy can guarantee more than 0.5 of the omniscient benchmark, which knows all arrival and departure times. Whether this guarantee is achievable has been a central open problem, even in special cases. We resolve this problem by showing that, on every instance, a simple static priority policy, which is computable in polynomial time, earns at least 0.5 of the omniscient benchmark. This establishes that the optimal competitive ratio is exactly 0.5, improving the previous best guarantee of 0.192 for the general model (Li et al. 2026, Collina et al. 2020). 

Our analysis rests on a key stochastic result, which is a new lower bound on the probability that some agent from a given set of types is available. Building on this bound, we develop two approaches: a primal approach that reads the priorities from an optimal solution of a novel linear program, and a dual approach that assigns a "value" to each type, and prioritizes matches with high "surplus" (reward minus value of involved agents). These values are the unique solution of a fixed-point equation derived from linear programming duality. We also show that the two approaches are closely connected.

detail.abstract: This paper transitions Constitutional Fault-Tolerance Theory (CFTT) from a conceptual framework to a quantitative mathematical model. By formalizing global geopolitical and institutional architecture as an undirected graph G = (V, E) with N = 9 strategic nodes, we construct an empirical 9 × 9 adjacency matrix. Using graph-theoretic metrics-including Betweenness Centrality (C B), Edge Connectivity (λ), Average Shortest Path Length (L), and a novel composite Constitutional Resilience Score (CRS)-we evaluate the systemic stability of the international order. We further model two dynamic stress scenarios: (1) the complete structural isolation of the Russian Federation (N 2), and (2) the strategic reorientation of the Global South (N 6) toward Western institutional architecture. Our findings demonstrate that node isolation yields a higher systemic resilience gain (+20.78% CRS) compared to path integration (+10.00% CRS), providing a mathematical basis for structural containment strategies in network security. Finally, we outline advanced theoretical extensions, incorporating multi-layer hypergraphs, high-frequency endogenous weight volatility, and game-theoretic adversarial edge rewiring coupled with an institutional 20% co-optation threshold theorem.

detail.abstract: I evaluate when a receiver's initial tritium requirement becomes a continuing external supply obligation. A serial aggregate fuel-cycle model gives a closed maintenance threshold in the inner-loop non-return fraction. For the declared parameters, loop decay and a maintained 1.944 kg reserve lower that threshold from 7.99 × 10-4 to 7.34 × 10-4. A 10-3 non-return fraction requires at least 0.757 kg/year of continuing receipts in the continuous-maintenance limit; fixed-cadence delivery adds storage and transit decay. A controlled comparison holds non-return fixed when varying reserves. I convert the full receiver trajectory into dated, batched requests and evaluate them against stochastic supplier histories, capacity constraints, customer priorities and qualification holds. Counterfactual pairs share the same operating appointments. The fixed 41-date benchmark supports no admissible start under its 1% total missed-commitment criterion; this is a result for the specified supply system, not a deployment forecast. Source replenishment and receiver needs are evaluated over matching horizons, while rejected tritium remains in the full-site inventory. Separate single-order experiments show the trade-off between incumbent protection and new-customer delay. The contribution is a reproducible interface from a declared fuel-cycle margin to customer-resolved supply commitments within established inventory theory. The computed values are conditional on an aggregate receiver model and synthetic supplier distributions; the tests support pre-feasibility screening, not operating authorization or a general self-sufficiency criterion.

detail.abstract: The integration of recommendation systems into modern transportation networks, from routing apps to mobility-as-a-service (MaaS) platforms, promises to enhance efficiency and reduce congestion. However, the success of these systems hinges on a critical human factor: user trust. This paper presents an agent-based model (ABM) to simulate the co-evolution of trust and compliance within a population of travelers interacting with a transportation recommendation system. The model represents travelers as heterogeneous agents with varying levels of initial trust, risk aversion, and sensitivity to recommendation outcomes (e.g., travel time savings or failures). The recommendation system, in turn, can employ different strategies, such as optimizing for individual versus system-wide benefits. We simulate repeated interactions where agents choose whether to comply with a recommendation, and based on the outcome, they update their trust level. Our findings reveal that the system's long-term adoption and effectiveness are not guaranteed, even when recommendations are technically optimal. We identify critical thresholds and feedback loops where a decline in trust leads to lower compliance, which in turn degrades the data quality needed for good recommendations, creating a negative spiral. The simulation demonstrates that strategies promoting transparency and consistently positive user experiences are crucial for building a resilient trust equilibrium. This research provides a foundational framework for designing more trustworthy and effective transportation recommendation systems by highlighting the dynamic interplay between algorithmic performance and human behavioral response.

title: Value Chain Addition and Benefits among Smallholder Farmers in North Eastern Uganda
affiliations: Makerere University, Makerere University, Makerere University and International Potato Center, Kampala, Uganda

detail.title: Value Chain Addition and Benefits among Smallholder Farmers in North Eastern Uganda
detail.abstract:
Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potato (OFSP) has significant potential to improve household nutrition, incomes, and rural industrialization through value addition. However, evidence on the uptake and sustained use of OFSP processing technologies among smallholder farmers in Uganda remains limited. This study assessed the status of OFSP value addition, examined processing technologies used by farmers, and analyzed the associated benefits and constraints in Kumi and Serere districts of North-Eastern Uganda. A cross-sectional survey involving 238 OFSP-producing households was conducted using structured questionnaires, key informant interviews, and focus group discussions. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics within the Value Chain Theory framework.,

Results showed that most farmers remained concentrated at the primary production stage, with 42.4% marketing raw tubers. Product upgrading was mainly reflected in the production of OFSP flour (49.8%) and chips (43.9%), while puree production remained low (2.2%). Process upgrading was constrained by high energy costs, operational difficulties associated with motorized chippers, and limited technical skills. Functional upgrading through packaging and distribution was evident but remained limited. Group membership and cooperative participation enhanced access to technologies, training, and markets.,

The study concludes that strengthening farmer organizations, promoting energy-efficient processing technologies, and expanding market opportunities are critical for advancing OFSP value-chain upgrading and commercialization.

detail.abstract:
We study NVIDIA cuOpt for continuous corporate-bond portfolio construction under spread and default risk, rating and issuer limits, duration matching, duration-times-spread bounds, and turnover constraints. The contribution is an open application benchmark, not a new optimization algorithm. We compare four endpoints: a raw first-order point, a feasibility-repaired point, a basic solution, and a directly modeled conic solution. A central case is a standard-deviation tracking-error target. A Gaussian-calibrated mean-absolute-deviation (MAD) proxy set to the same nominal budget delivers 28.5 bp against a ten-basis-point target, an overshoot of 2.85x. Recalibration is possible: a 2.25 bp MAD budget delivers 9.47 bp in-model and remains below target on 3 fixed validation draws. It requires a 4.44x nominal haircut, reduces the scaled objective by 13.6 bp, and increases CVaR loss by 4.43 bp relative to the exact SOCP portfolio. Thus the defect is not unavailability of the mandate but failure of naive calibration, with an observable cost-accuracy trade-off.

     Both conic solvers deliver the reference-size sigma mandate; working-size Clarabel remains feasible while the native cuOpt path records a crash. Contended SOCP timings are excluded. On the MAD-form LP, tight raw PDLP passes the proxy's numerical constraints without crossover, but this is not sigma compliance. A paired turnover leave-one-out and a matched-feasibility QP comparison show that constraint structure, representation, and solver endpoint matter alongside device choice. Results use a controlled credit scenario generator, not an empirical asset-pricing test or an executable bond-trading system. Supplemental pilots examine single-request timing and hypothetical bond-lot repair, retaining failed quality gates rather than reporting new speed advantages. Reported measurements are generated from archived result files.

detail.abstract: We study intraday market portfolio predictability in China across alternative forecast specifications and horizons, using lagged five-minute returns on 105 anomaly spreads. In the selected specification, the Standard Ensemble reduces out-of-sample squared forecast error relative to zero by 0.239% and 0.196% at 5- and 15-minute horizons, while evidence weakens at longer horizons. Trading Frictions characteristics account for the largest share of absolute fitted contributions in the selected linear ensemble. We assess the economic value of these forecasts by timing the CSI 300 ETF. In an ideal same-day simulation with an assumed 0.5 bp one-way fee, the positive multi-horizon rule attains a 0.602 Sharpe ratio, compared with 0.397 for matched passive exposure. Repricing the same positions at 1 bp turns the rule’s Sharpe negative. An exploratory lower-turnover rule is more resilient to fees, suggesting that harvesting the signal requires cost-aware rules and low execution costs. Market-state and policy-window comparisons do not identify a reliable setting in which the payoff survives. Trading costs and settlement constraints therefore prevent the current evidence from establishing an implementable net gain.

detail.abstract: Deep Hedging has been instrumental in sparking dedicated research into utilizing Neural Networks (NNs) to solve financial hedging and pricing problems that previously relied on closed-form analytical solutions. Traditional analytical frameworks rely on idealized assumptions regarding market mechanisms-particularly continuous trading, frictionless execution, and complete markets. Bridging the gap between these idealized models and real-world market frictions has been the foundational motivation behind Deep Hedging research. This paper formulates Deep Hedging as a metrics-driven, closed-loop information system spanning from initial path generation through production observability. We introduce methods for synthesizing training trajectories with controlled statistical characteristics alongside an information-theoretic measurement framework to evaluate both data richness and model efficacy across specific market regimes. Ultimately, this end-to-end approach equips trading desks with fine-grained control over the statistical distributions governing model training and provides a rigorous, experimental telemetry framework for deploying and iteratively refining Deep Hedging systems.

detail.abstract: The growing use of trade and technology restrictions for strategic purposes raises a central question for an increasingly fragmented world economy: do geoeconomic shocks sever international production linkages, or do global value chains reorganize around them? We study this question using the October 2022 U.S. export controls on advanced computing and semiconductor technologies directed at China. We assemble bilateral product-level trade data for 44 exporting economies and 226 importing economies over 2012-2024 and estimate gravity specifications using Poisson Pseudo-Maximum Likelihood. We distinguish four margins through which a geoeconomic technology shock can propagate: direct trade destruction, supplier substitution, geographic trade reallocation, and changes in product composition. The results point to reconfiguration rather than uniform trade destruction. U.S. semiconductor exports to China contract in value, with the decline concentrated in integrated circuits, while Japan and the Netherlands expand exports to China along important margins, particularly in semiconductor manufacturing machinery. Semiconductor trade also shifts toward alternative production and assembly hubs, although the response is heterogeneous across destinations and exporters. Finally, differences between changes in values, quantities, and unit values indicate compositional adjustment within continuing trade relationships. The findings show that the consequences of strategic technology restrictions extend beyond the directly targeted bilateral link: their incidence depends on technological specialization, substitutability across suppliers, and the capacity of third countries to absorb trade. These network responses are an important channel through which geoeconomic risk can reshape global production and the transmission of supply-side disturbances.

detail.abstract: The GENIUS Act of 2025 rewrites the priority and estate-property rules that govern the failure of a payment stablecoin issuer. It removes an issuer's required reserves from the bankruptcy estate and grants stablecoin holders a superpriority, capped at any reserve shortfall, over what remains. The commentary so far asks what happens inside bankruptcy once an issuer files-whether holders are actually paid and whether the case can be administered. This article identifies a different problem that arises before a filing. Because reserve assets leave the estate the moment they back a coin, a distressed firm can issue stablecoins to subordinate its existing creditors, hollow out the value a future administrator would need, and, when the firm is a bank, shift losses onto the deposit insurer and potentially the taxpayer. We call this stablecoin-on-creditor violence, drawing an analogy with the phenomenon of creditor-on-creditor violence that began with the 2016 J. Crew dropdown. Unlike in that episode, the stablecoin dropdown is on a statutory footing, meaning it is largely beyond the reach of the doctrines courts use to police its private-law cousins. We show that the subordination is accomplished by the rule carrying reserves out of the estate rather than by the celebrated superpriority. We raise concerns for financial stability: The threat of a dropdown grows with a firm's holdings of safe assets, meaning that creditors may respond negatively to a firm with a more liquid balance sheet. The harm is gravest when the subordinated creditor is the FDIC or another deposit insurer, because losses can be imposed on the rest of the financial system and the taxpayer. Importantly, the problems we raise do not rely on there being any investor demand for stablecoins. We close with a menu of responses and recommend a layered fix that federal regulators could largely implement on their own.

detail.abstract: This paper discusses how historical segregation impacts swimming access and water safety for the Black community in the United States, resulting in increased drowning risks for Black children and teenagers in particular. The research identifies and explores the concept of “swim deserts,” or areas where people lack easy access to safe public swimming, through multiple strategies: After a literature review summarizing existing data and analysis on drowning rates in the United States, including how drowning disproportionately impacts Black children, it discusses how historical policies governing access to swimming facilities have influenced this disparity and outlines the contemporary factors – such as income level, access to supervised water environments, and infrastructure – most strongly associated with elevated risk. Next, the paper combines historical analysis with quantitative modeling, including time-series analysis and regression techniques applied to national datasets. This enables better visualization of the nature and extent of drowning disparities, using charts and graphs to depict critical statistics. Ultimately, the research advocates for solutions that go beyond individual education, arguing that changes at the systemic level are necessary to combat the current inequities.

detail.abstract: Cultural heritage institutions are digitizing collections at a pace that outstrips the human capacity to describe, interpret, secure, and sustain them. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers powerful means of closing this gap through automated transcription, classification, restoration, three-dimensional reconstruction, and semantic search. Yet the same technologies introduce new risks, including algorithmic bias, misrepresentation of marginalized communities, opaque provenance, the exposure of sensitive cultural knowledge, and substantial energy demands. This article proposes the IES Framework (Intelligent, Ethical, Sustainable), a five-layer conceptual architecture for AIenabled digital heritage archives. The framework integrates governance and ethics, acquisition, intelligent processing, preservation and access, and sustainability monitoring, and is cross-cut by community participation and human oversight. Drawing on established standards such as the OAIS reference model, the FAIR and CARE principles, and UNESCO guidance, the article maps AI techniques to preservation tasks, identifies principal ethical risks with mitigation measures, and proposes sustainability indicators and a phased implementation roadmap. The central argument is that AI should be treated as an assistive, accountable component within long-lived archival systems rather than as an autonomous authority over cultural meaning. The framework is conceptual and is intended to guide institutions in designing, piloting, and evaluating AIsupported preservation programmes.

detail.abstract: Reported progress for foundation time-series models rests on comparisons that leave out a strong classical reference. Across eleven benchmark papers the classical arms are per-window refits of ETS, ARIMA and Theta; no online forecaster appears, and no suite scores a predictive density. We supply the missing reference: laplace, an online distributional forecaster with no pretraining and no tunable parameters. Scored one step ahead on held-out log density over an 18,815-series FRED panel, it beats TimesFM 3.0 on the median series of every stratum by about half a nat, and a post-hoc portfolio that sees only the model's own issued density recovers most of the gap. It is a pip install, with a Rust core and bit-exact parity.

detail.abstract: Affirmative action is usually judged by whether it raises outcomes for the group it designates relative to those it excludes. When the designated group is broad, that average can hide who the policy reaches. I study Malaysia's New Economic Policy (NEP), which from 1971 extended preferences to the Bumiputera category of the Malay majority and smaller indigenous groups. Using census data and a cohort differencein-differences design with the Chinese as the comparison group, I find that the NEP raised secondary-school completion among Bumiputeras in Peninsular Malaysia on average. That average reflects the Malay response. Relative to the Chinese, the Peninsula's other indigenous groups, mainly the Orang Asli, fell further behind, although their completion in absolute terms rose. These effects are concentrated in agricultural households and in districts where more of agriculture was in the cash crops rubber and oil palm, consistent with a higher opportunity cost of schooling. Outside agricultural households the two groups' gains are statistically indistinguishable. A single ethnic designation thus produced opposite-signed effects among its beneficiaries, and an evaluation at the level of the designated category would have missed it.

detail.abstract: This study develops a two-stage Mean-Conditional Value at Risk (Mean-CVaR) framework for container freight procurement using shipment-level costs and the Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI). The MATLAB implementation solves nine China-Northern Europe lanes using 2,000 scenarios and eight risk-aversion settings. At the primary setting λ = 1, volume-weighted modeled expected cost is EUR 635.07 per TEU, compared with EUR 962.78 for a feasible HistoricalMixPolicy, a conditional reduction of 34.04%. Relative to risk-neutral optimization, expected cost increases by 8.73% while the unweighted average of lane-level total-cost CVaR scaled by expected demand falls by 27.39%. Seven of 47 carrier-lane scenario models use accepted SCFI relationships and 40 use historical-cost fallbacks. Independent evaluation of the fixed primary contracts on a second 2,000-scenario sample supports limited within-model sampling stability, but does not establish historical predictive validity. The evidence therefore supports a modeled cost-risk trade-off, while scenario bounding, fallback calibration, assumed demandprice independence, contractual assumptions, and uncompleted historical validation remain important limitations.

detail.abstract: Rapid expansion of artificial intelligence has generated substantial investment in the physical hardware required to provide computing capacity. Yet conventional macroeconomic indicators, including trade statistics, reveal little about where the final economic value embodied in these systems is generated and captured. The paper addresses this gap by examining the NVIDIA GB200 NVL72, a rack-scale AI system with an estimated selling price of $3.3 million, by tracing the value embodied in the rack across its key supplying firms, production stages, and geographies, using calendar year 2025 as the baseline. Combining an estimated bill of materials with firm-level financial statements, the analysis is able to decompose nearly the entirety of the rack’s value added into six distinct components: labour compensation for (i) production and (ii) non-production workers; consumption of (iii) production and (iv) non-production capital; (v) corporate income taxes; and (vi) post-tax operating profit. The results reveal a concentrated distribution of value added. The fabless semiconductor company (NVIDIA) accounts for an estimated 67.0 per cent of the rack’s value added, followed by memory and storage suppliers (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron, Sandisk, Kioxia), at 6.7 per cent; the chip foundry (TSMC) at 4.9 per cent; and assembly and testing firms (Foxconn, Quanta, Wistron, Wiwynn) at 4.0 per cent. Across firms, post-tax operating profit represents 68.2 per cent of the traced value added, compared with 12.4 per cent for corporate income taxes, 14.0 per cent for labour compensation, and 5.3 per cent for capital consumption. Production labour alone accounts for only 4.1 per cent. Based on headquarters location, the geography of value added is concentrated primarily in the United States, the Republic of Korea and Taiwan Province of China. A simplified 2026 scenario nearly doubles memory suppliers’ share of rack value added, while NVIDIA remains dominant. The findings illustrate how the expansion of AI hardware can generate large trade flows while the associated value capture remains concentrated in a limited set of firms, functions, and economies. They have implications for trade and GDP measurement and for developing economies seeking to capture more value from participation in the AI hardware supply chain.
